elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a small nonzero value. With scl_i and sda_i released high, present cmd=START=4'b0001 while idle and hold the command until it is accepted. Continue clocking until cmd_ack is observed.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of shows: scl_oen participates in the corresponding timed bit-level SCL control sequence for the supported START command, including release of SCL during START setup and subsequent assertion of the active-low SCL drive enable for the low phase, followed by command completion.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare the observed scl_oen trace and clk_en-qualified phase transitions against a reference START bit-level sequence. Require the expected ordered release/drive transitions and a single cmd_ack; do not accept a permanently idle scl_oen trace.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a small nonzero value. Keep scl_i and sda_i released high, leave the controller idle, and present cmd=NOP=4'b0000 for multiple enabled timing ticks, then present an unsupported encoding such as cmd=4'b0011 for multiple enabled timing ticks.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting case of shows: scl_oen does not participate in a corresponding supported-command bit-level SCL control sequence when no supported command is presented. It remains in the idle released-line behavior, with no command phase progression and no cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen, idle, and cmd_ack across all driven NOP and unsupported-command cycles. Require no command-like scl_oen transition or timed SCL sequence, continuous idle behavior, and cmd_ack continuously low; compare against the same reference trace used for the supported-command case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue cmd=START=4'b0001 on a clock edge while idle, and hold cmd until the controller accepts it.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: after acceptance and before the one-clock cmd_ack pulse, start_sequence executes a timed START waveform on scl_oen and sda_oen: both lines are released, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released high, then SCL is driven low; cmd_ack asserts once and the controller returns idle.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model driven by clk_en to match the ordered scl_oen/sda_oen phases, allowing the modeled variable latency; assert that the sampled output-enable waveform matches the START sequence and that exactly one cmd_ack occurs before completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, keep the bus released high, issue cmd=STOP=4'b0010 while idle, and hold cmd until acceptance.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: after acceptance and before cmd_ack, stop_sequence drives SDA low, releases SCL and waits for filtered SCL high, then releases SDA while SCL is high; cmd_ack asserts once and the controller returns idle.
elements.check_method: Compare sampled scl_oen and sda_oen transitions with the STOP reference model at each enabled timing tick, including the required ordering and SCL-high wait; verify one completion pulse and no missing or extra phase.

elements.stimulus: Run two enabled WRITE transactions with clk_cnt=1 and a released-high bus: first issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100 with din=0, then issue the same command with din=1 after the first cmd_ack and return to idle.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: for each accepted WRITE, the timed sequence sets sda_oen according to din (0 drives SDA low; 1 releases SDA), releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low; the sequence advances only on enabled timing ticks and ends with one cmd_ack without arbitration loss when the external bus agrees.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for both din values and clk_en-gated phase progression; assert the expected sda_oen polarity, SCL release/drive ordering, stable-high phase, completion pulse, and absence of al.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1, set clk_cnt=1, have the external device return sda_i=0 for one READ and sda_i=1 for a second READ, issue cmd=READ=4'b1000 for each transaction while idle, and provide normal filtered SCL rising and falling edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: after each accepted READ, sda_oen remains released, scl_oen releases SCL for the read sampling window, the controller captures the filtered SDA value on the filtered SCL rising edge, then drives SCL low and asserts one cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Drive the synchronizer/filter reference model and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against the READ phase sequence; check that dout equals each returned filtered SDA value at the filtered SCL rising edge and that cmd_ack follows the low phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, remain idle and issue cmd=NOP=4'b0000 followed by unsupported cmd=4'b0011, holding each value for multiple enabled clocks while scl_i and sda_i remain high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: because no supported bit command is accepted, scl_oen and sda_oen do not follow any issued-command timed SCL/SDA pattern; they remain in the idle released state, no active command sequence occurs, and no cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Assert with an idle/no-op reference model that no command-specific output-enable transition occurs over the observation window and that cmd_ack remains low; distinguish this static idle waveform from the ordered phase waveforms required for supported commands.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, drive cmd=START while scl_i=1 and sda_i=1; keep the bus released-high until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the START command is accepted, sda_oen produces the SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase followed by the SCL-low phase, and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at completion.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the START phase sequence and compare sampled posedge traces of sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack; assert exactly one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1, drive cmd=NOP=0000 and then cmd=0011 while remaining idle, with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: neither unsupported/no-op command produces a START, STOP, WRITE, or READ sequence; scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the idle released state and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Compare all output-enable and cmd_ack cycles against the idle reference model; assert no command sequence and no acknowledgement pulse.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START, then while busy drive cmd=STOP with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1; keep the external bus high whenever the controller releases it.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: STOP drives SDA low, releases SCL, then releases SDA while filtered SCL is high; cmd_ack pulses once at completion and the filtered STOP transition clears busy.
elements.check_method: Check the ordered scl_oen/sda_oen trace, one-cycle cmd_ack, and busy transition against a cycle-accurate command and filtered-bus reference model.

elements.stimulus: With the controller idle and busy low, keep filtered SCL high and filtered SDA continuously high for 20 enabled clocks without issuing START or STOP.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: busy does not change because no filtered START or STOP transition occurs.
elements.check_method: Monitor busy and the filtered bus model; assert busy remains low throughout the no-transition interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, drive cmd=WRITE and din=0; provide a released-high external SCL and SDA and allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: WRITE drives SDA low through sda_oen for din=0, releases SCL for the high phase, drives SCL low for the low phase, and produces one cmd_ack without asserting al.
elements.check_method: Compare output-enable polarity and phase ordering with the WRITE reference model; assert cmd_ack is one clock and al remains low.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, drive cmd=WRITE and din=1; during the released SCL-high phase externally force SDA low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the expected-high WRITE bit loses arbitration; al asserts and remains asserted, the command aborts without cmd_ack, and both scl_oen and sda_oen release the bus.
elements.check_method: Detect the write stable-high phase, inject the wired-AND SDA disagreement, and compare al, cmd_ack, and both output enables with the arbitration-loss reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, drive cmd=WRITE and din=1; keep external SDA high during the released SCL-high phase and allow completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: arbitration remains intact, al stays low, the WRITE phase completes, and cmd_ack pulses once.
elements.check_method: Compare the released-high arbitration sample and terminal sequence to the reference model; assert no al and exactly one cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, drive cmd=READ; during the read sample window provide filtered SDA=0 and then repeat with filtered SDA=1, with filtered SCL rising once in each run.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: SDA remains released during READ, dout captures 0 and 1 respectively on the filtered SCL rising edge, SCL is subsequently driven low, and cmd_ack pulses once per completed READ.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-edge reference model to identify the read sample window and compare dout capture, sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack for both returned data values.

elements.stimulus: While idle, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0, then hold cmd=NOP; separately hold the controller idle with no command while toggling SDA without any filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: dout is not updated by the non-READ command or by SDA activity without a filtered SCL rising edge; it retains its prior value.
elements.check_method: Record dout before and after each stimulus and assert equality unless the reference model reports a filtered SCL rising edge during READ.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ with ena=1 and clk_cnt=2; when the controller releases SCL, hold scl_i low for several filter-sample intervals, then release scl_i high and return a stable SDA bit.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the controller enters slave_wait, does not advance the READ high-phase timing or generate cmd_ack while filtered SCL remains low, then resumes after filtered SCL becomes high and completes with the captured bit and one cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Check that scl_oen remains released while slave_wait is active, FSM phase and cmd_ack remain stalled, and completion occurs only after the filtered SCL-high condition.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ and, during a released SCL-high phase, hold external scl_i low indefinitely.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the command remains incomplete while the released SCL is filtered low; no later READ phase or cmd_ack occurs until the external clock stretch is removed.
elements.check_method: Run for a bounded number of enabled clocks while scl_i is held low and assert no phase advance beyond the stretch wait and no cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=WRITE with clk_cnt=2 and keep the controller's SCL released high; after filtered SCL is high, force an external SCL falling edge as another master would, then release it high again.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: multi-master synchronization detects the external falling edge, reloads timing, and restarts the local low-period timing; the command does not treat the unscheduled falling edge as a completed local phase.
elements.check_method: Observe scl_sync and compare the internal timing/reference-model counter reload and subsequent scl_oen phase ordering; assert no premature cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: With the bus filtered high and no active command, inject SDA and SCL raw-line pulses shorter than the filter sampling interval, then hold a valid SDA high-to-low transition while SCL is stably high for at least three filter samples.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for valid behavior and contrasting case for rejected glitches: short glitches do not change busy or al, while the stable filtered START sets busy; no false command status is produced by the glitches.
elements.check_method: Compare synchronized histories, majority-filtered values, detected START/STOP events, busy, and al to a three-sample filter reference model.

elements.stimulus: Start a WRITE command, then while it is active and not in a STOP sequence create a stable filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the unexpected filtered STOP is treated as arbitration loss; al asserts and remains sticky, the active command aborts without cmd_ack, and both output enables release.
elements.check_method: Inject the filtered STOP transition during active_command and compare al, cmd_ack, scl_oen, and sda_oen against the arbitration-loss model.

elements.stimulus: Run identical supported START, WRITE, and READ commands with ena=1 using clk_cnt=0, clk_cnt=1, and clk_cnt=16; provide stable bus responses and no stretching.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: all supported operations complete with their required phase ordering and one-cycle cmd_ack; total latency varies with clk_cnt but no command becomes stuck. scl_o and sda_o remain constant low while output enables control the bus.
elements.check_method: Use a parameterized divider/filter reference model to compare phase order, completion, cmd_ack width, and constant scl_o/sda_o across all prescaler values.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, then keep rst low and ena low/high as applicable while sampling reset and idle behavior. Model both external SCL and SDA as released high, and do not issue a command during the idle portion.
elements.expected_response: REQ-0003 shows-side: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen are 1 in reset and idle, releasing both open-drain lines so the modeled external lines remain high. No output port drives a high value.
elements.check_method: At asynchronous reset assertion and after every settled posedge through reset and idle, compare scl_o==0 and sda_o==0; compare scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1; resolve each modeled bus line as external_drive_low OR (output_enable==0) and require both lines high when externally released.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, clk_cnt=0, and both external lines initially high, issue a START command and allow it to complete, then issue a STOP command and allow it to complete. Record each registered output-enable value after every posedge.
elements.expected_response: REQ-0003 shows-side: during START/STOP command phases, scl_o and sda_o remain 0. When a line is to be driven low, its corresponding active-low enable is 0 and the resolved line is low; when released, its enable is 1 and the line may return high. START includes SDA driven low while SCL is released, followed by SCL driven low; STOP includes SDA driven low, SCL released, then SDA released while SCL is high.
elements.check_method: Use a phase-aware reference model for the START and STOP sequences. After each posedge, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against the expected drive/release phase; resolve bus levels with wired-AND open-drain semantics and verify the expected low/high phases and command acknowledgements.

elements.stimulus: During a command phase in which the DUT has released SCL and SDA, externally pull SCL low, SDA low, and then release them independently. Repeat during a phase in which the DUT drives each line low.
elements.expected_response: REQ-0003 contrasting-case check: an implementation that does not provide open-drain control would incorrectly drive a high value or fight an externally low line. The required DUT behavior is that scl_o and sda_o remain 0 at all times, scl_oen/sda_oen remain the sole drive-or-release controls, externally low lines stay low while the corresponding enable is 1, and a driven-low phase also remains low with enable 0; no DUT high drive or push-pull contention is observed.
elements.check_method: Monitor the resolved external lines and all four DUT ports on every settled posedge while toggling external low drives. Assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 unconditionally; when an enable is 1, require the resolved line to follow the external participant and never require a DUT high drive; when an enable is 0, require the resolved line low. Flag any high value on scl_o/sda_o or any line-high result while the DUT enable is 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the external SCL/SDA lines released high; issue a START command and observe the complete START sequence through its command acknowledgement.
elements.expected_response: At every sampled clock edge, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0. During the START phase that drives SDA low while SCL is high, sda_oen=0 and scl_oen=1; during phases that release a line, its corresponding output enable is 1. Thus 0 means the corresponding line is driven low and 1 means it is released. This is the holding side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, assert scl_o==1'b0 and sda_o==1'b0. Use the reference START phase sequence to compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the expected drive/release ownership and resolve the resulting open-drain line value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and issue a WRITE command with din=0, allowing the normal bit sequence to proceed with the external SCL line released high; capture both the SDA-low drive phase and the subsequent SCL/SDA release phases.
elements.expected_response: At every sampled clock edge, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0. In the WRITE phase where SDA must be driven low, sda_oen=0; in the released-high phases, sda_oen=1. When SCL is driven low, scl_oen=0, and when SCL is released, scl_oen=1. The contrasting release case is therefore explicitly distinguished from the drive case: 0 drives the corresponding line low, while 1 releases it.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking updates settle, assert both constant-low drive outputs. Correlate each observed output-enable value with the reference WRITE phase: require oen=0 for drive phases and oen=1 for release phases, and verify the open-drain bus model produces low when driven and high when released with no external pull-down.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1 while the external bus is released high; advance through the START sequence until the phase that drives SDA low while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: During the SDA-driven interval, sda_oen is low and the modeled SDA bus line is low. This is the low, pulled-low side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen against 0 and compute the open-drain bus level as low when sda_oen=0; flag any interval where the enable is high or the modeled SDA line is high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1 while the external SDA and SCL lines are released high; observe the initial START phase before the controller pulls SDA low.
elements.expected_response: During the initial released-SDA interval, sda_oen is high and the modeled SDA bus line is high from the external pull-up. This is the high, released side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen against 1 and compute the open-drain bus level with no external low drive; flag any interval where the enable is low or the modeled SDA line is not high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1 while the external SCL line is released high; advance through the START sequence until the phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: During the SCL-driven-low interval, scl_oen is low and the modeled SCL bus line is low. This is the low, pulled-low side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen against 0 and compute the open-drain bus level as low when scl_oen=0; flag any interval where the enable is high or the modeled SCL line is high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=1 with both external bus lines released high; observe the initial START phase and the interval before SCL is pulled low.
elements.expected_response: During the released-SCL interval, scl_oen is high and the modeled SCL bus line is high from the external pull-up. This is the high, released side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen against 1 and compute the open-drain bus level with no external low drive; flag any interval where the enable is low or the modeled SCL line is not high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue a supported START command on cmd, then wait until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen participates in the timed START bit-command sequence, including releasing SCL and subsequently driving SCL low before command completion; this is the `shows` behavior for the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked monitor to compare scl_oen against the reference START sequence and verify that it exhibits command-driven low/released phases before exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and apply NOP followed by each unsupported cmd encoding while the controller is idle.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: scl_oen does not exhibit a command-driven bit-level timing sequence; it remains in idle/released behavior, with no command completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen over the enabled clocks and assert it remains released high throughout each no-op interval, with no command-driven phase transitions and no cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START (4'b0001), and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Hold cmd until the command is accepted, then continue clocking through the complete START sequence.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for REQ-0007: during the active START command, scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen directly control the SCL and SDA lines through the START phases: both lines are initially released, SDA is driven low while SCL is released high, and then SCL is driven low before completion.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against a reference START-sequence model. Confirm that the externally modeled bus lines equal low whenever the corresponding enable is 0 and otherwise follow the released external-high level, with phase ordering matched to the observed start_sequence and clk_en probes.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Hold cmd until accepted and clock through the complete WRITE bit sequence.
elements.expected_response: This is an additional holding case for REQ-0007: the accepted WRITE command directly controls both line-control interfaces. scl_o and sda_o stay at 0; sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase and drives it low for the low phase, and the command eventually completes without arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model keyed by clk_en and the write_sequence/write_stable_high_phase probes. Check constant scl_o/sda_o values, active-low enable polarity, SDA ownership during the data phase, and SCL release/drive transitions at each WRITE phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=NOP (4'b0000) while the bus inputs are released high. Hold NOP for multiple enabled clocks, then repeat with unsupported cmd values 4'b0011, 4'b0101, and 4'b1111.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0007: because no supported command is accepted, no command-controlled SCL or SDA sequence occurs. scl_o and sda_o remain 0, scl_oen and sda_oen remain released high, and the controller remains idle rather than changing either line-control output.
elements.check_method: For every enabled clock during each NOP or unsupported-command interval, compare scl_o=0, sda_o=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1 against the reset/idle reference model; also verify the idle probe remains asserted and no output-enable transition occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, present cmd=START, and provide a released-high bus (scl_i=1, sda_i=1). Hold the command until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed port behavior: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen exhibit the START bit-level pattern: both lines are initially released, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released high, then SCL is driven low; cmd_ack is asserted once at completion.
elements.check_method: Use a reference phase model sampled after each posedge clk; compare the ordered registered scl_oen and sda_oen values and require exactly one cmd_ack pulse after the START sequence.

elements.stimulus: After a completed transaction, set ena=1 and present cmd=STOP with the bus initially active (scl_i=1, sda_i=0). Hold the command until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed port behavior: scl_oen and sda_oen exhibit the STOP bit-level pattern: SDA is driven low, SCL is released high, then SDA is released while SCL is high; cmd_ack is asserted once at completion.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered output-enable trace against the STOP phase model at each enabled timing tick and verify the single terminal cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and present cmd=READ with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1; allow the controller to run through one read bit until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed port behavior: sda_oen remains released for the read operation, scl_oen is released during the read sampling window and then driven low for the low phase, followed by one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Correlate scl_oen and sda_oen with the read_sequence and read_sample_window probes and compare every registered phase to the reference model until cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, din=0, and present cmd=WRITE with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1; allow the controller to complete the write bit.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed port behavior: sda_oen is driven low for the data-low phase corresponding to din=0, scl_oen is released for the write high phase and then driven low, and one cmd_ack pulse occurs at completion.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered output-enable sequence against the WRITE din=0 phase model, checking the stable-high phase and terminal cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, din=1, and present cmd=WRITE with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1; allow the controller to complete the write bit without external arbitration interference.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed port behavior: sda_oen is released for the data-high phase corresponding to din=1, scl_oen is released for the write high phase and then driven low, and one cmd_ack pulse occurs at completion.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered scl_oen/sda_oen trace against the WRITE din=1 phase model and verify completion with exactly one cmd_ack and no arbitration-loss abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and present an unsupported cmd value such as 4'b0011 for multiple enabled timing ticks; keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the observed port behavior: scl_oen and sda_oen do not exhibit any START, STOP, READ, or WRITE command-defined phase pattern; they remain in the released idle output state, no command sequence starts, and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Monitor the output-enable trace for the duration of the stimulus and compare it with an idle/no-operation reference model; assert no command-phase probe becomes active and no cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a SystemVerilog wrapper instantiating i2c_master_bit_ctrl and connecting clk, rst, nReset, and ena to one-bit signals and clk_cnt to a 16-bit signal; drive each connected input with both 0 and 1 values where applicable.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the interface observation: elaboration succeeds with clk, rst, nReset, and ena accepted as one-bit inputs and clk_cnt accepted as a 16-bit input.
elements.check_method: Require compilation and elaboration to complete without missing-port, direction, or width errors; use hierarchical port metadata or $bits checks to confirm $bits(clk)==1, $bits(rst)==1, $bits(nReset)==1, $bits(ena)==1, and $bits(clk_cnt)==16, with all five ports declared as inputs.

elements.stimulus: Compile the same structural wrapper with compile-time assertions requiring clk, rst, nReset, and ena to be one-bit input ports and clk_cnt to be a 16-bit input port; evaluate the wrapper against a DUT interface variant in which one required port is absent, has a non-input direction, or has a width other than specified.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of the interface observation: the structural check fails at compile or elaboration time rather than accepting the invalid interface as an implementation of i2c_master_bit_ctrl.
elements.check_method: Treat a missing-port diagnostic, direction mismatch, width mismatch, or failed static $bits/port-direction assertion as the required negative result; the check must fail for each injected interface defect.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the DUT using the required port list, driving cmd as a 4-bit input and connecting cmd_ack, busy, and al as single-bit output signals.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: interface inspection and elaboration succeed, with cmd declared as input [3:0] and cmd_ack, busy, and al each declared as one-bit outputs.
elements.check_method: Use a compile-time interface/signature checker or elaboration log to compare port names, directions, and widths against the contract; require no width, direction, or missing-port errors.

elements.stimulus: Run structural negative variants in which cmd_ack, busy, or al is omitted, declared as an input, or declared with a width other than one, and in which cmd is declared with a width other than four or with the wrong direction.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the interface must be identified as not satisfying the requirement; compilation, elaboration, or the dedicated interface checker must reject or flag each malformed declaration rather than accepting it as a conforming DUT.
elements.check_method: Apply mutation-based compile/elaboration tests and assert that each changed port name, direction, or width produces the expected structural mismatch diagnostic.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT and inspect its declared port list, including the din and dout declarations.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout is present as a one-bit output port, and din is present as a one-bit input port.
elements.check_method: Use compiler/elaboration reflection or the generated HDL interface metadata to assert dout direction=output and width=1, and din direction=input and width=1.

elements.stimulus: Run the interface checker against negative interface variants in which dout is omitted, declared with a width other than one bit, or declared as an input, and in which din is omitted, declared with a width other than one bit, or declared as an output.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: the interface checker rejects each variant because dout is absent, has a different width, or is not an output, or because din is absent, has a different width, or is not an input.
elements.check_method: Compile/elaborate each mutated interface and require a structural port-contract failure; record the specific missing, width, or direction mismatch.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT and inspect the module interface metadata for port scl_o.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_o is declared as a one-bit output port at the module interface.
elements.check_method: Use simulator/VPI or elaboration metadata to compare the declared direction and width of scl_o against output, width 1; fail on any other declaration.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate a negative-control DUT variant in which scl_o is omitted or declared as an input or inout port, while applying the same interface inspection.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_o is not declared as an output port, so the interface check must reject the variant.
elements.check_method: Run the structural interface checker and require a direction-mismatch or missing-port failure for scl_o.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT and inspect the module interface metadata for scl_oen; then connect it to a one-bit external net for an I2C transaction.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen is declared as a one-bit output port serving as an active-low output enable, with low meaning the DUT drives SCL low and high meaning the DUT releases SCL.
elements.check_method: Check interface direction and width through elaboration metadata, then compare the observed SCL line against the open-drain bus model for scl_oen=0 and scl_oen=1 during driven and released phases.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate a negative-control DUT variant in which scl_oen is omitted, declared as an input or inout, or documented/implemented with active-high enable semantics.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen is not an output port serving as an active-low output enable, so the interface/behavior check must reject the variant.
elements.check_method: Require structural direction or port-presence failure for declaration mismatches, and require an active-low polarity failure when scl_oen=0 releases SCL or scl_oen=1 drives it low.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT and inspect the module interface metadata for port sda_o.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sda_o is declared as a one-bit output port at the module interface.
elements.check_method: Use simulator/VPI or elaboration metadata to compare the declared direction and width of sda_o against output, width 1; fail on any other declaration.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate a negative-control DUT variant in which sda_o is omitted or declared as an input or inout port, while applying the same interface inspection.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: sda_o is not declared as an output port, so the interface check must reject the variant.
elements.check_method: Run the structural interface checker and require a direction-mismatch or missing-port failure for sda_o.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT and inspect the module interface metadata for sda_oen; then connect it to a one-bit external net for a START, WRITE, and released-SDA phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sda_oen is declared as a one-bit output port serving as an active-low output enable, with low meaning the DUT drives SDA low and high meaning the DUT releases SDA.
elements.check_method: Check interface direction and width through elaboration metadata, then compare the observed SDA line against the open-drain bus model for sda_oen=0 and sda_oen=1 during driven and released phases.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate a negative-control DUT variant in which sda_oen is omitted, declared as an input or inout, or documented/implemented with active-high enable semantics.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: sda_oen is not an output port serving as an active-low output enable, so the interface/behavior check must reject the variant.
elements.check_method: Require structural direction or port-presence failure for declaration mismatches, and require an active-low polarity failure when sda_oen=0 releases SDA or sda_oen=1 drives it low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena high and issue a supported START, STOP, READ, or WRITE command with a bus response that allows normal completion. Drive clk with multiple rising edges and observe cmd_ack through the terminal command phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: cmd_ack asserts on the rising edge of clk following command completion and remains asserted for exactly one clk cycle before deasserting.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, compare cmd_ack with a reference command-completion model; require the first assertion to occur only on the specified rising edge, remain high for one clock interval, and be low on the following rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Repeat a supported command to completion while toggling clk continuously, and sample cmd_ack immediately after each posedge and negedge clk, including the interval before completion, the completion edge, and the following clock edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case of shows: cmd_ack does not change state away from a rising edge of clk and does not remain asserted for more than one clk cycle; it must not assert on a falling edge or persist across successive rising edges.
elements.check_method: Use an edge-sensitive assertion that cmd_ack is stable between successive posedges of clk and that any high interval is bounded by one adjacent rising-edge period; flag any negedge transition, mid-cycle transition, or consecutive-cycle assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported START command while the bus is released high. Allow the command to progress through its completion phase using a modeled clk_en schedule, then continue for at least two additional rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: cmd_ack changes state only immediately after a rising edge of clk, remains stable between rising edges, and is asserted for exactly one clock interval when the START command completes.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, sample cmd_ack after registered updates settle; monitor cmd_ack continuously between adjacent rising edges and assert it has no transitions except at the sampled edge. Assert that the completion indication is one full clock wide.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a supported WRITE command with ena=1 and valid din. During an active command and again during the expected completion interval, change cmd and din at times strictly between rising edges of clk; keep clk running and permit normal command timing to reach completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of shows must not occur: cmd_ack must not change state between rising edges of clk and must not produce a completion pulse with boundaries off the rising-edge grid. Input changes between edges may affect a later sampled operation, but cannot cause an asynchronous cmd_ack transition.
elements.check_method: Use a continuous waveform assertion that every cmd_ack transition occurs at a posedge clk, and compare each pulse's rising and falling boundaries with successive posedges. Fail if cmd_ack changes during any inter-edge interval or if its pulse is not exactly one clock interval.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high and ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, issue a WRITE command with din=0, and wait until write_sequence is active with sda_oen=0. Assert rst=1 before a rising edge of clk and sample outputs after that edge.
elements.expected_response: On the synchronous reset edge, scl_oen and sda_oen become 1, cmd_ack is 0, busy is 0, and al is 0. The active command is abandoned and both open-drain lines are released.
elements.check_method: At the post-edge sampling point, compare scl_oen, sda_oen, cmd_ack, busy, and al against the reset-state scoreboard; verify that no command-completion pulse occurs on the reset edge.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the WRITE setup with nReset high, ena high, clk_cnt=0, din=0, and wait until write_sequence is active with sda_oen=0. Keep rst=0 through the corresponding rising edge of clk and continue clocking with the bus otherwise valid.
elements.expected_response: With synchronous reset not asserted, the command phase remains governed by normal operation: sda_oen is not forced to 1 by reset, the active command continues, and cmd_ack may be generated when the WRITE completes. busy and al retain their ordinary pre-existing values.
elements.check_method: Compare the no-reset trace with the command-phase reference model, checking that the output enable is not reset-forced and that normal command completion can produce cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high and ena high, establish a busy bus by driving a stable filtered START condition externally: keep scl_i high and transition sda_i from high to low long enough for synchronization and filtering to detect it. After busy becomes 1, assert rst=1 before a rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge with rst asserted, busy becomes 0, cmd_ack is 0, al is 0, and the reset-defined released interface is present with scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered START detection and busy output to establish the precondition, then sample all five observable ports immediately after the synchronous reset edge and compare with the reset scoreboard.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the external stable filtered START sequence until busy becomes 1, then keep rst=0 and keep the bus free of a STOP condition for multiple rising edges of clk.
elements.expected_response: Without synchronous reset, busy remains 1 while no clearing event occurs; it is not reset to 0. cmd_ack and al retain their ordinary values, and output enables remain governed by normal bus/FSM behavior rather than being forced to the reset state.
elements.check_method: Monitor busy over the no-reset interval and compare it with a reference model that holds busy until STOP or reset; verify no reset-state transition occurs.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, ena high, and clk_cnt=0, issue WRITE with din=1. During the released SCL-high WRITE phase, externally hold SDA low long enough for filtered arbitration loss to be detected. After al becomes 1, assert rst=1 before a rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: On the synchronous reset edge, al becomes 0, cmd_ack remains 0, busy becomes 0, and scl_oen and sda_oen are 1. Reset clears the sticky arbitration-lost status and leaves the interface released.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered arbitration-loss indication to establish al=1, then compare all observable ports after the reset edge with the reset-state scoreboard and verify no acknowledgement pulse is produced.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the din=1 WRITE arbitration-loss sequence until al becomes 1, then keep rst=0 and provide no reset input while clocking several rising edges.
elements.expected_response: With rst low, al remains 1 because no synchronous reset clears it; it is not changed to 0 by ordinary clocking. cmd_ack remains suppressed for the aborted command, while output enables and busy follow their normal post-arbitration-loss behavior rather than reset behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor al across multiple rising edges and compare against a sticky-status reference model; verify that no reset-state transition or command acknowledgement occurs.

elements.stimulus: With clk running, rst low, ena high, and the controller in a non-reset operating state, assert nReset low at a time between two rising edges and hold it low. Do not apply another clk edge before sampling the outputs.
elements.expected_response: As the holding case of observed_via.shows, immediately after nReset falls and before any subsequent clock, the resettable state is asynchronously initialized: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, and dout=0. These values must not wait for clk.
elements.check_method: Sample all listed outputs immediately after the asynchronous nReset assertion using an event-region-safe observation, and compare against the reset reference model before the next posedge. Verify the transition occurs without a clock edge.

elements.stimulus: Deassert nReset high between rising edges while rst remains low, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and the filtered bus is released high. Confirm the controller is idle, then issue cmd=START and keep the bus released-high while supplying subsequent clk edges.
elements.expected_response: As the non-holding case of observed_via.shows, deasserting nReset must not asynchronously initialize or alter scl_oen; it remains governed by the current clocked FSM state. After the next enabled clock accepts START, scl_oen and sda_oen change only according to the normal START sequence and registered FSM timing, with no asynchronous reset-style transition on nReset deassertion.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and sda_oen around the between-clock nReset rising edge and require no reset-driven change. Then compare each subsequent output-enable value at posedges with a reference START-sequence model, checking that changes occur only on clocked state updates.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 1 and hold the bus released high. With ena high, issue a supported WRITE command, wait until the command is accepted and write_sequence is active, then drive ena low for at least 8 rising edges while holding cmd at NOP and keeping external SCL high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen remains at the current timed WRITE phase value throughout the ena-low interval; the FSM does not advance to the next SCL control phase and no command completion occurs solely due to elapsed clocks while ena is low.
elements.check_method: At every rising edge during the ena-low interval, compare scl_oen and the active-command/phase probe against a sampled pre-disable value; assert that no scl_oen transition or cmd_ack pulse occurs until ena is restored high.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 1 and hold the bus released high. With ena high, issue the same supported WRITE command and keep ena high after acceptance until the command completes, with cmd set to NOP after acceptance.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: scl_oen advances through the WRITE command's timed SCL phases on enabled timing ticks and the command eventually reaches its terminal phase and produces the normal one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use a reference timing model to predict clk_en ticks and expected WRITE phase order; compare each observed scl_oen transition and the single cmd_ack pulse against that model, allowing the specified registered output latency.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the bus released, create a filtered START by holding SCL high and transitioning SDA from high to low long enough for synchronization and majority filtering; wait until busy is high. Then drive ena low and create a filtered STOP-shaped input by transitioning SDA from low to high while holding SCL high, maintaining the transition for more than one filter interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy remains high while ena is low; filter progression is gated, so the STOP-shaped raw input does not produce a filtered STOP or clear busy during the disabled interval.
elements.check_method: Sample busy, sscl, ssda, sto_condition, and the filter sampling probe after each rising edge; assert busy remains high and sto_condition remains inactive throughout the ena-low interval despite the stable external STOP-shaped input.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and the bus released, first create and filter a START transition so busy becomes high. Then transition SDA from low to high while holding SCL high and maintain the STOP-shaped input long enough for the synchronizer and majority filter to process it, without deasserting ena.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: the input filter progresses while ena is high, the STOP transition becomes filtered, and busy clears to low after the registered STOP-processing update.
elements.check_method: Compare the synchronized samples, filter-history/majority result, sto_condition, and registered busy output against a reference filter model; require busy to transition high-to-low after the expected filtering and registered-output latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt to 3 and ena high long enough for the divider and filter timing to begin. Then drive ena low and hold it low for at least 8 rising edges of clk while keeping scl_i and sda_i stable.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for REQ-0018: while ena is low, the clock divider is reloaded rather than progressing toward expiry, filter_cnt is reset, clk_en remains low on every clock, and no normal bit-timing or filter progression occurs.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered updates settle, compare clk_en, filter_cnt, and the divider state against a reference timing model. Assert that clk_en is never asserted and that filter_cnt remains at its reset value throughout the ena-low interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt to 3, keep ena high, and hold scl_i and sda_i stable for enough rising edges to span multiple divider intervals and filter sampling intervals.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ena-not-low case: the divider progresses and expires according to clk_cnt, clk_en is asserted at modeled expiry points, and filter_cnt is allowed to progress and produce filter sampling events instead of being continuously reset.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the divider and derived filter interval. Compare observed clk_en and filter_cnt/filter sampling behavior after each posedge, requiring at least one modeled clk_en assertion and corresponding normal timing progression while ena remains high.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd3, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=START and keep cmd stable until completion.
elements.expected_response: The divider loads cnt from clk_cnt and produces clk_en ticks at the reference-model cadence. The START FSM advances only on those clk_en ticks, rather than on every system clock, and eventually reaches its terminal phase and asserts cmd_ack for one clock.
elements.check_method: Sample clk_en, idle, start_sequence, and cmd_ack after each posedge. Compare tick timing and FSM advancement against a reference divider model that reloads cnt with 3 and decrements only while ena is high; verify no FSM phase transition occurs without a corresponding clk_en tick and verify exactly one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=START and keep cmd stable until completion.
elements.expected_response: The zero prescale value is loaded into cnt without a stuck or wrapping divider. clk_en is generated on every enabled clock according to the defined zero-reload behavior, allowing the START FSM to advance and complete with a one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare cnt_zero and clk_en on every enabled posedge with a reference model treating clk_cnt=0 as an immediate-expiry reload. Check that clk_en does not remain permanently low, that START progresses on successive ticks, and that one cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set clk_cnt=16'd3 and ena=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=START, and keep ena low for at least 10 rising edges before raising ena.
elements.expected_response: When the requirement does not hold because the core is disabled, clk_en remains low, the divider does not advance command timing, and the START FSM does not progress or acknowledge. After ena is raised, divider timing resumes and clk_en ticks allow the pending command to advance.
elements.check_method: Sample clk_en, cnt_zero, idle, start_sequence, and cmd_ack after each posedge. Assert no clk_en pulse, counter expiry, FSM transition, or cmd_ack during the disabled interval; then compare resumed tick cadence after ena rises with the reference divider model for clk_cnt=3.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd8, hold scl_i and sda_i stable high, and run posedge clk cycles long enough to observe multiple filter sampling events.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: filter_cnt derives the SDA/SCL filter sampling interval from clk_cnt; with clk_cnt=8, the filter sampling interval is floor(8/4)=2 enabled clocks, so filter_cnt expires and synchronized samples are shifted into the filter histories at the corresponding cadence.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare filter_cnt expiration and fscl/fsda sample-shift events against a reference model using filter_interval=floor(clk_cnt/4)=2. Confirm that the measured interval between successive filter sampling events is two enabled clocks.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd0, hold scl_i and sda_i stable high, and run consecutive posedge clk cycles with no ena stall.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: when clk_cnt=0, the derived filter interval does not create a stalled or invalid filter counter; filter_cnt expires on every enabled clock and synchronized SDA/SCL samples are shifted into the filter histories on every enabled clock.
elements.check_method: Compare filter_cnt and fscl/fsda events cycle by cycle with the reference model's zero-interval rule. Confirm one filter sampling event per enabled clock and no interval longer than one clock or stuck filter progression.

elements.stimulus: After reset, wait until the command FSM is idle, set ena=1, present cmd=4'b0001 (START), and hold cmd at that encoding until the command sequence completes while scl_i and sda_i are released high.
elements.expected_response: Holding the supported bit-level command causes the command sequence to be accepted and completed; cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle. This is the positive side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on every posedge after registered outputs settle; assert that exactly one high pulse occurs after command acceptance, that it is one clock wide, and that no additional pulse occurs for the same command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, wait until the command FSM is idle, set ena=1, present cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) and hold it for multiple enabled clocks; repeat with cmd=4'b0011, an unsupported 4-bit encoding.
elements.expected_response: Neither NOP nor the unsupported encoding is accepted as a command: cmd_ack remains low throughout and no command-complete pulse is generated. This is the negative side of the observed shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample cmd_ack on every posedge while each command value is held and for the following observation window; compare against a zero-pulse expectation and assert that the FSM remains idle with no cmd_ack high cycle.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, wait until the FSM is idle, then drive cmd=4'b0001 (I2C_CMD_START) through an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: while idle, cmd=I2C_CMD_START is decoded as START, and on the enabled timing tick sda_oen transitions from 1 to 0 while scl_oen remains 1, producing the START-condition signature.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered updates settle, assert idle before command acceptance and compare the waveform against a reference model: detect a 1-to-0 sda_oen transition on a clk_en tick with scl_oen still 1; record a coverage hit and require no contradictory command-decode result.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, wait until the FSM is idle, and separately drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) and each unsupported encoding 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, and 4'b1111 for enabled clock ticks.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case of the requirement: with the FSM idle and cmd equal to NOP or an unsupported encoding, sda_oen does not transition from 1 to 0 as a START signature, while scl_oen remains released high and the FSM remains idle.
elements.check_method: For every listed command, sample sda_oen and scl_oen after each posedge and compare with the idle/NOP reference model; require no 1-to-0 sda_oen transition attributable to command acceptance, no START-sequence probe assertion, and no command-complete pulse.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, then set ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. After reset initialization leaves the command FSM idle, drive cmd=4'b0010 (I2C_CMD_STOP) and hold it through an enabled clock tick; keep the bus externally released high throughout the STOP sequence.
elements.expected_response: The STOP command is accepted from idle and executes its STOP sequence. On completion, cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock and then returns low with no additional pulse. This is the holding side of the observed shows statement: cmd_ack pulses high for one clock when STOP completes.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after reset, compare cmd_ack against a reference STOP-command model. Require one and only one high sample after the STOP terminal phase, require the pulse width to be one clock, and require no pulse before acceptance or after that clock.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, then set ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. After reset initialization leaves the command FSM idle, drive cmd=4'b0000 (I2C_CMD_NOP) and hold it through several enabled clock ticks; do not issue a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: The non-STOP command is not accepted as a STOP command, no STOP sequence occurs, and cmd_ack never pulses. This is the contrasting side of the observed shows statement: when the STOP-command requirement does not hold, cmd_ack does not pulse for the presented command.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack and the command-sequence observables on each posedge clk for the complete observation window. Compare against a no-ack reference model and require cmd_ack=0 on every sampled clock, with no STOP-sequence activity.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the FSM idle, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and released-high bus lines, drive cmd=4 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) for an enabled idle acceptance tick, then drive cmd=0. Set din=0 and keep the bus released during the resulting WRITE data-bit phase until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd=4 selects the WRITE operation, and during its data-bit phase sda_oen is 0 because din=0; the WRITE sequence subsequently completes with its command acknowledgement.
elements.check_method: Use the idle and write_sequence probes to identify command acceptance and the data-bit phase; compare the sampled registered sda_oen waveform against din=0 and verify that cmd_ack occurs after the WRITE phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the FSM idle, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and released-high bus lines, drive cmd=4 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) for an enabled idle acceptance tick, then drive cmd=0. Set din=1 and keep the bus released during the resulting WRITE data-bit phase until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd=4 selects the WRITE operation, and during its data-bit phase sda_oen is 1 because din=1; the WRITE sequence subsequently completes with its command acknowledgement.
elements.check_method: Use the idle and write_sequence probes to identify command acceptance and the data-bit phase; compare the sampled registered sda_oen waveform against din=1 and verify that cmd_ack occurs after the WRITE phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the FSM idle, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and released-high bus lines, drive cmd=0 (I2C_CMD_NOP) for an enabled idle acceptance tick while toggle din between 0 and 1 over subsequent enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: because cmd is not I2C_CMD_WRITE, no WRITE data-bit phase occurs, sda_oen does not follow din as WRITE data output behavior, and no command acknowledgement is generated.
elements.check_method: Use the idle and write_sequence probes to confirm that no WRITE sequence is entered; monitor sda_oen while toggling din and verify it remains at the idle released value rather than changing according to din, with cmd_ack low.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and while idle drive cmd successively to NOP=0000 and each unsupported value 0011, 0101, 0110, 0111, 1001, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, and 1111 for an enabled clock; return cmd to NOP between trials.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: for every NOP or unsupported cmd value, idle remains asserted and the FSM does not enter any command sequence.
elements.check_method: At every enabled posedge after each command value is applied, sample the idle probe and compare it with a reference FSM; require idle=1 throughout each trial and no transition to read_sequence.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold the bus released high, and while idle drive cmd=READ=1000 through an enabled posedge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting, condition-false case: the FSM does not remain idle; it starts the READ sequence, with idle deasserting and read_sequence becoming active.
elements.check_method: Use a transition monitor on successive settled posedge samples to verify idle=1 before READ acceptance, then idle=0 and read_sequence=1 after the enabled command-acceptance tick.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), hold din=0 through command acceptance and the WRITE data-bit phase, and model the external SCL/SDA lines as released high except for DUT drive.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit transmission phase, before the corresponding SCL high phase, sda_oen is 0. This is the din=0 side of the required behavior: SDA is driven low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while write_sequence is active for the data-bit phase and before the SCL high phase, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference value 0; flag any mismatch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), hold din=1 through command acceptance and the WRITE data-bit phase, and model the external SCL/SDA lines as released high except for DUT drive.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit transmission phase, before the corresponding SCL high phase, sda_oen is 1. This is the din=1 side of the required behavior: SDA is released high.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while write_sequence is active for the data-bit phase and before the SCL high phase, compare the registered sda_oen output against the reference value 1; flag any mismatch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE), din=1'b0, and provide a released-high SCL bus so the command is accepted and write_sequence becomes active. Keep din=0 until cmd_ack or abort.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-drive phase while write_sequence is active, sda_oen is 0. This is the din=0 holding side of the requirement: SDA is driven low through the active-low open-drain enable.
elements.check_method: At every clock while write_sequence is asserted and before cmd_ack or abort, compare the registered sda_oen output against 0; record a failure if it is not 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE), din=1'b1, and provide a released-high SCL bus so the command is accepted and write_sequence becomes active. Keep din=1 until cmd_ack or abort, and do not externally pull SDA low during the released-high phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-drive phase while write_sequence is active, sda_oen is 1. This is the contrasting din=1 side of the requirement: SDA is released high rather than driven low.
elements.check_method: At every clock while write_sequence is asserted and before cmd_ack or abort, compare the registered sda_oen output against 1; record a failure if it is not 1.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena high and a valid clk_cnt, issue a READ command while the external I2C bus is released high, and keep scl_i high throughout the READ sample window.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case from REQ-0028: the received external SCL at scl_i is high, so the READ bit cycle completes and cmd_ack asserts as a single one-clock pulse after the READ low phase.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_i, the READ/sample-window probe, and cmd_ack on settled posedge observations. Compare against a READ reference model and verify exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs after the high sample window and no extra pulses occur.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena high and a valid clk_cnt, issue a READ command, and externally hold scl_i low after the controller releases SCL for the READ sample window. Keep scl_i low for multiple enabled timing opportunities, then release it high.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case from REQ-0028: while the received external SCL remains low, cmd_ack does not pulse and READ completion is postponed. After scl_i is released high and the filtered SCL becomes high, the READ cycle completes and cmd_ack asserts as a single one-clock pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_i, filtered SCL, the read_sample_window/slave_wait probes, and cmd_ack on settled posedge observations. Assert no cmd_ack during the low-SCL interval, then compare the post-release completion and one-clock pulse against a clock-stretching READ reference model.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset, release it, set ena=1 and a valid clk_cnt, issue READ, then model the external SCL line as held low after the DUT releases scl_oen=1. Keep scl_i low long enough to pass synchronization and majority filtering, then drive scl_i high and keep it high through the filter interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the READ sampling window, scl_oen remains 1 and the READ phase does not proceed to drive SCL low until the synchronized and filtered SCL becomes high; after filtered SCL becomes high, the phase proceeds and scl_oen transitions to 0 at the normal timed end of the sampling window.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer, three-sample majority filter, divider, and READ FSM. Assert that scl_oen is released while filtered SCL is low, that no low-drive transition occurs before the modeled filtered-high point, and that the subsequent transition occurs at the modeled enabled timing point.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset, issue READ with ena=1, release SCL through scl_oen=1, and hold scl_i low for the entire observation window so that no synchronized and filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen remains 1 and the READ phase remains waiting; it must not proceed to drive SCL low while filtered SCL has not become high.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and the READ phase timing against a reference model with a permanently-low synchronized/filter input. Fail if scl_oen becomes 0 or the READ command advances without a modeled filtered SCL high.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, issue START while scl_i is stably high, and drive sda_i high then low long enough for the synchronized and majority-filtered SDA to fall while the synchronized and filtered SCL is high. Then drive sda_i low then high while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the filtered START condition, busy becomes high; after the filtered STOP condition, busy becomes low. Transitions must occur from filtered, synchronized line values rather than directly from raw scl_i.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of both synchronizer/filter pipelines and the filtered START/STOP equations. Compare busy transitions cycle-by-cycle to the modeled filtered conditions and allow only the registered output latency.

elements.stimulus: Start with busy low and stable filtered SCL low. Apply SDA transitions and short raw scl_i/sda_i glitches that do not survive the two-stage synchronization and three-sample majority filter; subsequently apply a stable SDA transition while filtered SCL remains low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: busy remains unchanged; a raw SCL/SDA glitch or SDA transition while filtered SCL is low must not produce a START or STOP indication or change busy.
elements.check_method: Predict synchronized samples, filter histories, filtered SCL/SDA, and START/STOP detections with a reference model. Assert that busy has no transition for every injected glitch and for SDA transitions occurring while modeled filtered SCL is low.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue READ with ena=1, arrange for scl_i to be low before the sampling window, then drive scl_i high and keep it high until the synchronized and filtered SCL has a rising edge. Drive sda_i to 0 for one test and 1 for a second test at the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout updates to the filtered SDA value, respectively 0 and 1, on the registered cycle that processes the filtered SCL rising edge; the value must reflect filtered SDA rather than an unsynchronized raw sample.
elements.check_method: Run a cycle-accurate synchronizer/filter/reference READ model and compare dout after each posedge with the modeled filtered SDA captured at the modeled filtered SCL rising edge, including the specified one-cycle registered observation behavior.

elements.stimulus: Issue READ and keep scl_i low throughout the sampling window, or apply only raw SCL pulses too short to survive synchronization and majority filtering. Change sda_i between 0 and 1 during the window without allowing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: dout does not capture a new SDA sample and retains its prior value because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that the synchronized/filter histories never generate a filtered SCL rising edge. Assert that dout remains stable throughout the READ window despite raw SDA changes and rejected raw SCL glitches.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command with ena high and a released-high bus. Connect sda_i to a modeled external I2C SDA pad/top-level open-drain buffer, return a stable 0 for one transaction and a stable 1 for a second transaction, and provide the corresponding filtered SCL rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0030: sda_i acts as the external SDA line input from the pad or top-level open-drain buffer, and dout captures the synchronized, majority-filtered SDA value (0 or 1 respectively) on each filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage sda_i synchronizer, filter sampling, three-sample majority, and filtered SCL rising-edge detection; compare dout after the registered update with the modeled SDA value and verify the expected READ completion.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same READ transactions, but drive sda_i directly from an independent testbench SDA driver rather than through the modeled external pad or top-level open-drain buffer; return the same stable 0 and 1 values at the same filtered SCL rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for REQ-0030: even when sda_i is not modeled as being sourced by the external pad or top-level open-drain buffer, dout still captures the same synchronized and filtered SDA value at the filtered SCL rising edge; the port-source topology does not alter the observed READ result.
elements.check_method: Run the same synchronizer/filter reference model and compare dout cycle-by-cycle against the holding-case results for identical sda_i line values and filtered SCL edges; require identical captured values and completion behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i high and sda_i high long enough to initialize the synchronized and three-sample filtered histories. Then drive sda_i low and hold it through at least two-stage synchronization and enough filter sampling intervals for filtered SDA to make a high-to-low transition while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for busy: busy asserts only after the filtered SDA START transition is detected, demonstrating that busy responds to synchronized and filtered SDA rather than the raw input transition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SDA synchronizer, filter sampling, majority result, and delayed SDA edge detection; compare the modeled START detection and busy output after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: With scl_i high, establish busy low and stable filtered SDA high. Pulse sda_i low for less than the synchronization/filter interval, then return it high before the filtered three-sample history can represent a high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for busy: busy does not change because the short SDA transition is not presented by the synchronized and filtered signal as a START or STOP condition.
elements.check_method: Predict synchronized samples, filter histories, majority output, and START/STOP edges with the reference model; assert that no filtered SDA edge qualifying with filtered SCL high occurs and busy remains unchanged.

elements.stimulus: First create busy high using a filtered START sequence. While scl_i remains high, drive sda_i high and hold it through synchronization and filter settling so filtered SDA makes a low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for busy: busy clears when the synchronized and filtered SDA STOP transition is detected with filtered SCL high.
elements.check_method: Compare busy against a reference model of synchronized SDA, majority filtering, delayed filtered SDA, and STOP detection; require the clear to occur only at the modeled filtered STOP event.

elements.stimulus: Create busy high with a valid filtered START, keep scl_i high and filtered SDA low, then pulse sda_i high for less than the filter interval before returning it low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for busy: busy remains high; the raw SDA pulse does not clear busy because synchronization and filtering do not present it as a STOP condition.
elements.check_method: Use the synchronizer/filter reference model to verify that filtered SDA has no qualifying low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high, then compare the registered busy output.

elements.stimulus: Issue a WRITE command with ena high and din=1. Allow the FSM to reach the released SCL-high stable WRITE phase. Keep external scl_i high and drive sda_i low long enough for the synchronized and filtered SDA value to become low during sda_chk.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for al: al asserts during the WRITE arbitration-check phase because filtered SDA is low while the master expects released SDA high; the command aborts and no command-complete pulse is produced.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for command phase timing, SDA synchronization/filtering, stable-high arbitration checking, and abort behavior; compare al, cmd_ack, and output enables after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: Issue a WRITE command with din=1 and reach the released SCL-high stable WRITE phase. Pulse external sda_i low for less than the synchronization/filter interval, then release it high before filtered SDA becomes low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for al: al does not assert and the WRITE is not aborted, because the SDA pulse is not represented by the synchronized and filtered SDA value as arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Model the two-stage capture and majority filter, verify filtered SDA remains high throughout the arbitration check, and compare al, cmd_ack, and command completion against the model.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command with ena high. During the read sample window, release SCL and drive sda_i to 0, holding it long enough for synchronization and filtering to settle before the filtered SCL rising edge. Repeat with sda_i held at 1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for dout: dout updates at the filtered SCL rising edge to the synchronized and filtered SDA value, capturing 0 in the first read and 1 in the second.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the synchronizer pipeline, filter histories, filtered SCL rising edge, and read sample window; compare dout only at the modeled filtered rising edge and verify both data values.

elements.stimulus: Issue a READ command and establish a known dout value. Drive a short SDA pulse, or change sda_i outside the READ sampling window, so the raw input changes but the synchronized/filter output does not produce a qualifying SDA value at a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for dout: dout does not update from the raw or filtered-out SDA change outside the READ sampling event; it retains its previous value until a qualifying filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to determine synchronized and filtered SDA history and filtered SCL rising edges; assert no dout update for the injected pulse/out-of-window transition and compare the registered dout value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=START, clk_cnt=0, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Apply the START command on a clock edge and continue supplying the released-high bus until the START sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the START command reaches its completion edge, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and is low on the immediately preceding and following cycles.
elements.check_method: A clocked scoreboard detects START command acceptance and its terminal completion event, then compares cmd_ack on three consecutive settled posedge samples against 0, 1, 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish a busy transaction context, then set ena=1, cmd=STOP, clk_cnt=0, and provide a released-high SCL bus. Apply the STOP command and allow its SDA-low, SCL-release, and SDA-release phases to reach the terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the STOP command finishes, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle only.
elements.check_method: The reference model identifies the STOP terminal phase and checks the registered cmd_ack waveform is a single-cycle pulse with no assertion before completion or after the following clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=READ, clk_cnt=0, keep SDA released, and drive the external bus through a complete read bit: release SCL high, present a stable filtered SDA value, allow the filtered SCL rising edge to be observed, then allow SCL to return low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the READ low phase and terminal completion edge, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and then deasserts.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-edge reference model to identify READ completion, and compare cmd_ack at the completion edge and adjacent clock cycles to require a 0-to-1-to-0 pulse.
