elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE, din=0, clk_cnt=0, and provide a released-high bus with SDA remaining low when driven. Allow the WRITE sequence to set SDA, release SCL for the high phase, pull SCL low, and reach its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the WRITE command completes normally, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle only.
elements.check_method: The scoreboard tracks the WRITE terminal phase and checks cmd_ack is low before completion, high for the completion cycle, and low on the next cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE, din=1, clk_cnt=0, and begin a WRITE with the bus released high. During the stable released SCL-high phase, externally hold SDA low so filtered SDA becomes low and arbitration loss is detected before the normal terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: the WRITE command aborts on arbitration loss and cmd_ack does not assert at the abort event or on any subsequent cycle for that command.
elements.check_method: Detect the filtered arbitration-loss event and compare cmd_ack from that event through return to idle; require it to remain 0, while separately confirming al becomes asserted and both lines are released.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 with no external stretching. Present START while idle and run clocks until the START sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the START command finishes, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle. It is low before the terminal completion cycle and low again on the immediately following cycle.
elements.check_method: Use a command-sequence reference model to identify the terminal START phase, then sample cmd_ack after each posedge and assert the exact pulse-width and one-cycle timing relationship.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=STOP, and keep the external bus released high with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. First establish a busy transaction context, issue STOP from idle, and run clocks until the STOP sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle when the STOP command reaches its terminal phase, remains low during all earlier STOP phases, and returns low on the next clk cycle.
elements.check_method: Correlate the observed scl_oen and sda_oen phase sequence with a STOP reference model and compare cmd_ack on every clock against the model's terminal-phase completion event.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ, and provide a released-high SCL bus. During the READ sample window drive sda_i=0, then allow the read bit cycle to proceed through its low phase to completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle after the READ bit-level command finishes. cmd_ack remains low during command execution and is low again immediately after its single completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered SCL rising-edge and READ phase model to determine completion, then assert that cmd_ack is one registered pulse aligned with that event and absent on all other cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE, din=0, and keep scl_i=1 with the external SDA line low only when driven by the DUT and otherwise high. Issue WRITE while idle and run the complete write bit sequence without arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle when the WRITE command reaches its terminal phase, with no cmd_ack during intermediate write phases and no pulse after the completion cycle.
elements.check_method: Track the write phase sequence and terminal event in a reference model, and compare the sampled cmd_ack waveform to a one-cycle pulse at that event with low values before and after.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=3, cmd=START, and keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Issue START while idle, then sample cmd_ack during an identified intermediate START phase before the prescaler permits the terminal phase, and continue running until completion.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: while the START command has not finished and the FSM is in an intermediate bit-level phase, cmd_ack remains low. Only after the later terminal phase does cmd_ack produce the single one-cycle completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the divider and FSM reference model to mark an intermediate nonterminal cycle and the eventual terminal cycle; assert cmd_ack=0 at the intermediate observation and assert exactly one pulse at completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, release both open-drain bus lines high, then drive SDA from high to low while holding SCL high long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to produce a filtered START condition. Keep the bus active without generating a filtered STOP.
elements.expected_response: This is the busy side of the requirement: busy asserts high on the registered cycle that processes the filtered START condition and remains high throughout the interval before a filtered STOP.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronization, filter sampling, majority value, and START detection. Compare busy after each posedge against the model and require busy=1 after filtered START detection with no intervening filtered STOP.

elements.stimulus: Generate a filtered START as in TP-0000, then while SCL is high drive SDA from low to high and hold the transition long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered STOP condition. Continue holding the bus released and idle.
elements.expected_response: This is the not-busy side of the requirement: busy clears low on the registered cycle that processes the filtered STOP condition and remains low during the subsequent idle interval.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-signal reference model to identify the STOP edge, then compare the registered busy output after each posedge. Require busy=0 after filtered STOP detection and throughout the following idle interval.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, set rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0. Hold filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high, then drive SDA low while SCL remains high for enough enabled clocks to produce a filtered SDA falling edge and sta_condition=1. Do not generate a STOP condition afterward.
elements.expected_response: On the registered update corresponding to sta_condition=1, busy becomes high and remains high while no filtered STOP condition occurs. This is the high-after-START side of the requirement's shows statement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking updates settle, compare the busy output with the sta_condition and sto_condition probes. Require busy=1 on the cycle after filtered START detection and throughout the subsequent interval with sto_condition=0; verify with a scoreboard sampled over the complete scenario.

elements.stimulus: Reset and configure the DUT as in TP-0000. First create a filtered START by holding SCL high and transitioning SDA from high to low long enough for sta_condition=1. After busy is high, hold SDA low while SCL remains high, then transition SDA from low to high for enough enabled clocks to produce a filtered STOP and sto_condition=1.
elements.expected_response: busy becomes high after the filtered START, then becomes low on the registered update corresponding to sto_condition=1 and remains low while no subsequent START is detected. This is the low-after-STOP side of the requirement's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Use the sta_condition and sto_condition probe pulses as reference events and sample busy after each posedge settles. Assert busy=1 after the START event and busy=0 after the STOP event, with no extra busy transitions between them.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so busy starts low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and keep filtered SCL and SDA stable high for multiple enabled clocks. Do not apply any filtered SDA transition while filtered SCL is high, so neither sta_condition nor sto_condition asserts.
elements.expected_response: busy retains its prior low state when neither a filtered START nor a filtered STOP condition is detected. This is the otherwise side of the requirement's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Monitor sta_condition and sto_condition probes for the entire stable-bus interval and compare busy on every settled posedge against its pre-stimulus value. Require no busy transition and busy=0 throughout.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a START command until it completes. Issue WRITE with din=1. During the WRITE stable high phase, when sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, externally hold SDA low so filtered SDA ssda=0; continue clocking through the detection edge and subsequent clocks.
elements.expected_response: At the arbitration-loss detection edge, the observed al output rises to 1, which is the asserted side of the requirement's shows condition. al remains 1 on subsequent clocks until either reset input is asserted; the aborted command does not produce cmd_ack and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare al against a reference model that detects ssda=0 while sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1 during an active WRITE. Assert that al transitions from 0 to 1 on the detection edge and remains 1 until reset; separately check that no cmd_ack occurs for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a START command until it completes. Issue WRITE with din=1. During the WRITE stable high phase, when sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, leave the external SDA line released/high so filtered SDA ssda=1; allow the WRITE command to complete normally.
elements.expected_response: Throughout the active WRITE and after its completion, the observed al output remains 0, which is the deasserted side of the requirement's shows condition, because no arbitration loss is detected. The WRITE completes with one cmd_ack pulse and al does not assert.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare al with a reference model for the no-loss case: during each arbitration-checking high phase, ssda must remain high and al must remain deasserted. Check that al stays 0 through command completion and that the normal cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset to clear al, release reset, keep ena high, and issue START. After START completes, issue WRITE with din=1. During the WRITE stable high phase, when sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, externally drive sda_i low long enough for the synchronized and majority-filtered ssda to become 0 while scl_i remains high.
elements.expected_response: The arbitration-loss condition is met: al asserts on the registered observation and remains asserted after the injected low SDA condition. This is the holding case of observed_via.shows: al asserts and remains asserted.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization and filtering to identify the first sda_chk=1 cycle with sda_oen=1 and ssda=0; compare the sampled al output on that and all subsequent clocks, and verify it remains high until reset.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset to clear al, release reset, keep ena high, and issue START. After START completes, issue a non-STOP command such as READ. While active_command=1, externally create a stable filtered STOP by allowing filtered SCL to remain high and driving SDA from low to high long enough for sto_condition=1; do not issue a STOP command from the controller.
elements.expected_response: The unexpected STOP condition is detected during the active non-STOP command, so al asserts on the registered observation and remains asserted. This is the holding case of observed_via.shows: al asserts and remains asserted.
elements.check_method: Monitor active_command and the reference-model sto_condition derived from filtered SDA/SCL transitions; compare al immediately after the detected unexpected STOP and on every following clock until reset.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset to clear al, release reset, keep ena high, and issue START. After START completes, issue WRITE with din=1. During the WRITE stable high phase, allow sda_oen=1 and sda_chk=1 while externally keeping SDA high so filtered ssda remains high; throughout the active command, keep SDA/SCL transitions free of any filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: Neither arbitration-loss activation condition occurs, so al does not newly assert and remains low through normal command completion. This is the contrasting case of observed_via.shows: al does not newly assert as a consequence of either activation condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm every arbitration-checking phase has ssda=1 and no unexpected sto_condition occurs while active_command=1; compare al on each clock and verify it remains 0 through cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset, release the bus, set ena=1, issue the READ command cmd=1000, and complete the READ setup until the read sampling window releases SCL high. Drive the external SDA line so that the filtered SDA value is 0, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge while the READ sampling window is active.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the registered update corresponding to the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures and equals the filtered SDA value 0.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of synchronization, filter histories, majority filtering, and filtered-edge detection. At each modeled filtered SCL rising edge during read_sample_window, sample dout after nonblocking assignments settle and compare it with the modeled filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset, release the bus, set ena=1, issue the READ command cmd=1000, and reach a READ interval in which filtered SCL remains low with no filtered SCL rising edge. Change the external SDA value so the filtered SDA changes from 0 to 1 while filtered SCL remains low, then hold SCL low for several enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout does not update to the changed filtered SDA value and retains its previous value 0.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that no filtered SCL rising edge occurs during the interval. Sample dout after each enabled clock and assert that it remains unchanged despite the filtered SDA transition; separately verify that an update is only permitted on a modeled filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset asynchronously, release it, then apply synchronous rst and leave the module idle with ena low and high in turn; vary scl_i, sda_i, cmd, and clk_cnt while observing scl_o.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o remains continuously 0 throughout reset, idle operation, and input changes. Any observed 1 or transition is the otherwise side and fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked and asynchronous-reset-aware assertion that scl_o === 1'b0 at all sampled times, including immediately after nReset assertion and after each posedge; record any high value or transition.

elements.stimulus: With nReset released and ena high, execute START, WRITE with din=0 and din=1, READ, and STOP using clk_cnt values 0, 1, and a larger value; include clock stretching, arbitration-free bus activity, ena pauses, and reset between transactions while observing scl_o on every clock.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o remains continuously 0 during every command phase, timing tick, stall, pause, completion, and reset. The otherwise side of shows is scl_o high or changing value; either observation is a failure.
elements.check_method: Compare the full scl_o waveform against a constant-zero reference at every posedge and during asynchronous nReset transitions, independent of command phase and variable latency; fail on any nonzero sample or edge.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a START command with the external SCL and SDA lines released high. Wait for the START sequence to reach its SCL-low phase where scl_oen=0.
elements.expected_response: Holding-side case: scl_o remains exactly 1'b0 while scl_oen=0, and the resulting open-drain SCL line is driven low by the output-enable control rather than by scl_o.
elements.check_method: At every posedge during the SCL-low phase, compare scl_o against constant 0 and independently compute the bus SCL level from scl_oen and the external driver; require scl_o==0 and bus SCL==0.

elements.stimulus: Continue the same enabled START transaction until the START sequence releases SCL, with scl_oen=1; keep the external SCL participant released so the physical SCL line is high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting control-side case: scl_o remains exactly 1'b0 even while scl_oen=1, and the SCL line is high because scl_oen releases the open-drain line; scl_o must not be used to control the line level.
elements.check_method: During the released-SCL phase, compare scl_o against constant 0 and compare the observed bus SCL level with the open-drain model for scl_oen=1 and no external low driver; require scl_o==0 and bus SCL==1.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START, and clock until the START sequence reaches its SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: During the SCL-low phase, scl_oen is 0; this is the asserted-low side of the requirement and commands the open-drain SCL driver to drive SCL low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_oen against the START-phase reference model and require scl_oen==0 when the model indicates the SCL-low phase; also verify the externally modeled SCL line is low.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START, and clock until the START sequence reaches a phase in which SCL is released before it is driven low.
elements.expected_response: During the SCL-released phase, scl_oen is 1 rather than 0; this is the otherwise side of the requirement, so the output-enable does not command the open-drain SCL driver to drive SCL low and the externally modeled SCL line remains high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_oen against the START-phase reference model and require scl_oen!=0 (specifically 1) in the release phase; verify the external line is not driven low by the DUT.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, then clock the DUT with rst=0, ena=1, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue a START command with cmd=0001 and clk_cnt=0, and observe the initial START phase in which the controller releases both bus lines.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: at the clocked interface observation, scl_oen=1, so SCL is released for the external pull-up, and sda_o=0, the constant-low SDA drive value.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen to 1 and sda_o to 0; additionally model the open-drain SCL line and verify that with no external low drive it is high.

elements.stimulus: From an active START command begun with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the external bus released-high and clock until the START sequence reaches its subsequent SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: at the clocked interface observation, scl_oen=0, so scl_oen is not 1 and SCL is not released; independently, sda_o remains 0 as the constant-low SDA drive value.
elements.check_method: Use the clocked output trace to identify the START phase transition, then assert scl_oen=0 and sda_o=0 in the low phase; model the open-drain SCL line and verify it is low when the DUT drives it.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=START, and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Wait for command acceptance and advance through the START sequence until the phase that pulls SDA low while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sda_o is 1'b0 at every observation, sda_oen becomes 1'b0 during the SDA-low phase, and the modeled SDA bus line is low because sda_oen, rather than sda_o, controls the open-drain drive.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, assert sda_o==1'b0; compare the modeled open-drain SDA line against sda_oen, requiring line=0 when sda_oen=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=READ, and hold the external SDA/SCL lines high. Advance through the READ command to its read sampling window, where SDA is released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting release case: sda_o remains 1'b0, sda_oen becomes 1'b1 during the READ sampling window, and the modeled SDA bus line rises high through the external pull-up; SDA control is therefore provided by sda_oen while sda_o remains constant low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, assert sda_o==1'b0; when sda_oen==1'b1 with no external SDA pull-down, assert the modeled SDA line is high, and verify that changing the external pull-down changes the line without changing sda_o.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, release the external SDA and SCL lines high, and issue cmd=START while idle. Observe the START sequence through its phase that pulls SDA low while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during the SDA-low phase, sda_oen is 0 and the resolved open-drain SDA line is driven low despite the external participant releasing SDA.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare sda_oen to the reference START sequence and monitor the resolved SDA bus level with the external SDA driver released; require sda_oen==0 and resolved SDA==0 during the SDA-low phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, release the external SDA and SCL lines high, and issue cmd=READ while idle. Observe the READ sequence during its SDA-released read bit window.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: during the SDA-released read window, sda_oen is 1 and SDA is released rather than driven low, so the resolved SDA line remains high when the external participant also releases it.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare sda_oen to the reference READ sequence and monitor the resolved SDA bus level with the external SDA driver released; require sda_oen==1 and resolved SDA==1 during the read window.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high, and issue a START command. Observe the initial START phase in which the controller has not yet pulled SDA low.
elements.expected_response: The sda_oen output is 1; this is the holding case of REQ-0045, so SDA is released and the external pull-up drives the SDA line high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the START sequence, compare sda_oen against the expected phase value and resolve the open-drain SDA line with an external pull-up model; require sda_oen=1 and SDA high during the release phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, keep the external SDA and SCL lines released high, and issue a WRITE command with din=0. Observe the data-drive phase before SCL is released for the write bit.
elements.expected_response: The sda_oen output is 0; this is the otherwise side of REQ-0045's observed_via distinction, so SDA is driven low rather than released for the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the WRITE data phase, compare sda_oen against the expected active-low enable polarity and resolve the open-drain SDA line; require sda_oen=0 and SDA low despite the external pull-up.

elements.stimulus: Perform specification-to-testplan traceability review for implementation detail 1; apply no DUT inputs and do not initiate a transaction.
elements.expected_response: The DUT has no required runtime response for REQ-0046@1; no command acceptance, state transition, output change, status change, or timing behavior is attributed to this requirement.
elements.check_method: Static review confirms REQ-0046@1 has no declared activation, observable output, or behavioral effect and that the testbench contains no runtime check attributed to it.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, hold it across a clock edge, deassert it, then assert rst high for one rising edge and release it. Leave ena low and then high while issuing no command; keep scl_i and sda_i high.
elements.expected_response: During asynchronous reset, synchronous reset, and subsequent idle operation, scl_o and sda_o are continuously 1'b0. This is the shows side: the outputs remain constant low and never directly drive SCL or SDA high. Any scl_o=1 or sda_o=1 is the otherwise side and fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_o and sda_o immediately after every clock edge and at asynchronous nReset assertion; use assertions that each value equals 1'b0 throughout reset and idle. Record any nonzero sample as a failure.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, clk_cnt set to 0, and a released-high external bus, issue START, wait for completion, issue WRITE with din=0 and then din=1, issue READ while externally returning both 0 and 1 on separate transfers, and issue STOP. Also apply clock stretching and arbitration-loss conditions while observing all command phases.
elements.expected_response: Across idle, START, STOP, WRITE, READ, clock-stretch, and arbitration-loss phases, scl_o and sda_o remain 1'b0 on every observation; only scl_oen and sda_oen may control open-drain line ownership. This is the shows side. If either output becomes 1 during any phase, that is the otherwise side—direct high drive or loss of the constant-low assignment—and the test fails.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked assertion sampled after nonblocking updates: @(posedge clk) scl_o===1'b0 && sda_o===1'b0, with additional samples during reset and command-boundary transitions. Correlate failures with the active command and verify that external bus levels are produced only by the output-enable/open-drain model.

elements.stimulus: After asynchronous reset is released, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, provide a released-high bus, issue the START command, and sample the START phase in which SDA is driven low while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: For the SCL side of the requirement's low-drive case, scl_oen is 0 and scl_o remains constant 0; the resolved SCL line is pulled low. For the SDA side, sda_oen is 0 and sda_o remains constant 0; the resolved SDA line is pulled low. This is the low side of the corresponding observed_via shows statements.
elements.check_method: At every registered output update in the START sequence, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0, compare each output-enable value against the expected phase, and calculate the open-drain resolved line as low when oen==0 and otherwise the externally released level.

elements.stimulus: After completing START, issue STOP with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 on a bus with no external participant pulling either line low; sample the STOP phase after SCL is released and while SDA is released to complete STOP.
elements.expected_response: For the SCL side of the requirement's high-release case, scl_oen is 1 and scl_o remains constant 0; the resolved SCL line is released and therefore high. This is the high side of the SCL observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: During the STOP release phase, assert scl_o==0, assert scl_oen==1, and compare the resolved SCL line against high with the external pull-up enabled and no external low drive.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue START, and sample the phase in which the controller pulls SDA low while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: For the SDA side of the requirement's low-drive case, sda_oen is 0 and sda_o remains constant 0; the resolved SDA line is pulled low. This is the low side of the SDA observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: At the registered START drive phase, assert sda_o==0 and sda_oen==0, and calculate the resolved SDA line with an external released-high bus to confirm it is low.

elements.stimulus: After completing START, issue STOP with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 on a bus with no external low drive, then sample the final STOP phase after SDA is released while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: For the SDA side of the requirement's high-release case, sda_oen is 1 and sda_o remains constant 0; the resolved SDA line is released and therefore high. This is the high side of the SDA observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: During the final STOP release phase, assert sda_o==0, assert sda_oen==1, and compare the resolved SDA line against high with the external pull-up enabled and no external low drive.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus, then issue a valid START command while clk_en permits the START sequence to begin.
elements.expected_response: During the START sequence's released-line phase, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1. The external open-drain bus model must resolve both SCL and SDA high through pull-ups. This is the 'shows' side for both observed ports.
elements.check_method: At each registered output update, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the reference sequence and resolve each bus line as high when its enable is 1 and no external device drives it low; require both resolved lines to be high during the release window.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus released high, issue a valid WRITE command with din=0 and advance through the command until the WRITE low phase in which SDA is driven low.
elements.expected_response: In the WRITE phase that drives the data bit low, sda_oen=0, so the controller pulls SDA low rather than releasing it for the external pull-up. This is the contrasting 'otherwise' side for sda_oen.
elements.check_method: Use a phase-aware reference model to identify the WRITE data-low phase; sample sda_oen after the posedge and require 0, then verify the open-drain bus model resolves SDA low despite the pull-up.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus released high, issue a valid START command and advance through its sequence until the phase that pulls SCL low after SDA has been asserted low.
elements.expected_response: In the START low-clock phase, scl_oen=0, so the controller pulls SCL low instead of releasing it for the external pull-up. This is the contrasting 'otherwise' side for scl_oen.
elements.check_method: Use the START phase probe/reference model to identify the SCL-low phase; sample scl_oen after the corresponding posedge and require 0, then verify the open-drain bus model resolves SCL low.

elements.stimulus: Run the DUT through synchronous and asynchronous reset, then hold ena=1, cmd=0000 (NOP), and stable bus inputs; classify this test instance as the case where the list-number marker "2." is present.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of this requirement: no hardware behavior is required and no output, including cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_oen, or sda_oen, is constrained by REQ-0050. The DUT may exhibit only behavior required by other requirements.
elements.check_method: Record the marker-present bin and apply no REQ-0050-specific output assertion; confirm that the checker does not fail for any observed DUT output because this requirement has no observable expectation.

elements.stimulus: Run the DUT through synchronous and asynchronous reset, then issue a supported command with ena=1 and stable bus inputs; classify this test instance as the contrasting case where the list-number marker "2." is absent.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of this requirement: no hardware behavior is required and no output, including cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_oen, or sda_oen, is constrained by REQ-0050. There is no REQ-0050-specific difference at any port.
elements.check_method: Record the marker-absent bin and apply no REQ-0050-specific output assertion; confirm that any observed command behavior is checked only against its owning requirement and is not attributed to REQ-0050.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high, rst low, and ena high. Set clk_cnt to 3. After initialization and a counter reload, leave all inputs unchanged for successive posedges until the counter reaches zero, then continue for another reload interval.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of the requirement: on cycles where reset, ena-low, cnt_zero, and scl_sync are all inactive, cnt decrements and clk_en remains deasserted; when the counter expires, clk_en asserts for the expiration cycle and cnt reloads from clk_cnt.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare the observed clk_en probe against a reference divider model initialized and reloaded to 3; require no clk_en pulse during ordinary decrement cycles and one pulse on each modeled expiration.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, rst low, and ena high, set clk_cnt to 5. Assert rst high across a posedge, keep it high for one additional posedge, then deassert rst while leaving the other inputs unchanged.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for reset: while reset is active, cnt is loaded from clk_cnt and clk_en is asserted rather than following the ordinary decrement path. After reset is deasserted, the divider resumes from the reloaded value and clk_en follows the normal expiration schedule.
elements.check_method: Sample clk_en after each posedge and compare cnt/expiration behavior with a reference model that gives rst priority and reloads cnt to 5 with clk_en asserted during reset.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 4, hold nReset high and rst low, first run with ena high, then drive ena low for three consecutive posedges, and finally drive ena high again.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for core disabled: on every cycle with ena low, cnt is reloaded from clk_cnt and clk_en is asserted; no ordinary decrement progression occurs. When ena returns high, timing resumes from the reloaded counter value.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed clk_en probe each cycle with a reference model that reloads cnt to 4 and asserts clk_en whenever ena is low, checking that the disabled interval contains no decrement-based timing sequence.

elements.stimulus: Run the divider with ena high, rst low, and nReset high using clk_cnt values 0, 1, and 16'hffff in separate trials. For each trial, allow enough enabled posedges to observe at least two timing events.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for cnt reaching zero: each modeled expiration reloads cnt from the selected clk_cnt and asserts clk_en. clk_cnt=0 must not stall; it produces clk_en on every enabled clock. clk_cnt=1 produces the corresponding minimum nonzero reload cadence, and 16'hffff produces the long cadence without premature pulses.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for each reload value and compare every observed clk_en pulse, including zero and one boundary cases, against the model.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to 4. With reset released and ena high, issue a START command and then a READ command so the controller reaches a phase where SCL is released high; while the master is released, externally pull scl_i low to create a filtered SCL falling edge and hold it low long enough to assert scl_sync.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for multi-master synchronization: when scl_sync occurs, cnt is reloaded from clk_cnt and clk_en is asserted, restarting timing from the synchronization event rather than continuing the ordinary decrement sequence. The command timing then remains paused or synchronized until filtered SCL permits progress.
elements.check_method: Correlate the scl_sync and clk_en probes with the reference divider model; require a reload/assertion at the synchronization event and verify subsequent timing uses a fresh reload interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=START for acceptance, and model the bus as released-high for SDA but externally hold SCL low. Keep scl_i=0 long enough for the synchronized and majority-filtered sSCL to remain low after the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1), and maintain the condition for multiple enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: This is the slave_wait=1 side of the observed behavior: while the released SCL remains filtered low, the timing counter does not decrement or reload, clk_en remains low, the command FSM does not advance, and cmd_ack remains low with no completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model or internal assertion to compare cnt across consecutive posedges while slave_wait=1 and require it to remain unchanged; simultaneously sample slave_wait, clk_en, scl_oen, and cmd_ack after each posedge, requiring slave_wait=1, clk_en=0, scl_oen=1, and cmd_ack=0 throughout the wait interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=START for acceptance, and model the bus as released-high with scl_i=1 so that filtered sSCL reaches high and slave_wait does not assert. Allow the command to run through its normal terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the no-slave-wait side of the observed behavior: the timing counter advances normally and produces clk_en ticks, the FSM proceeds through the START sequence, and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock when the command completes.
elements.check_method: Compare sampled clk_en and command-state progression against a reference model with no stretching; assert that slave_wait remains 0, timing ticks occur, and cmd_ack has exactly one rising interval followed by low, with no acknowledgement suppressed or indefinitely postponed.

elements.stimulus: Present the third implementation-details item to the verification review and execute the DUT under its normal regression stimuli without adding any behavior-specific stimulus for this item.
elements.expected_response: No DUT output, state transition, timing relationship, or protocol behavior is required or expected as a consequence of this item.
elements.check_method: Review the requirement-to-test trace and confirm the item has no associated DUT assertion or behavioral pass/fail condition; record the check as satisfied when no unrequested behavior is inferred.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported READ command (cmd=1000) on a clk_en-enabled idle cycle. Model the bus as open-drain, keep scl_i low continuously, and allow the command to reach the phase where scl_oen is released high; hold scl_i low long enough for the synchronized and majority-filtered sSCL to remain low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in which SCL has just been released through scl_oen=1 while filtered SCL remains low: slave_wait asserts, the controller remains waiting, and the READ sequence does not advance through the SCL-high phase until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the slave_wait probe and READ-phase progression with a reference model of scl_oen, the two-stage SCL synchronizer, three-sample majority filter, and wait condition (scl_oen=1 && sSCL=0). Bin an observed assertion of slave_wait while the condition holds and verify no phase advance while it remains asserted.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the enabled READ sequence from reset, but drive scl_i high continuously before and throughout the phase where the controller releases SCL through scl_oen=1. Keep the line high long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to make sSCL high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case in which SCL is released and filtered SCL is high: slave_wait remains deasserted, the controller does not enter a slave-wait hold, and the READ sequence may proceed through its high-phase sampling window on subsequent timing enables.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the slave_wait probe and READ-phase progression with the same reference model. Specifically verify that after scl_oen becomes 1 and sSCL becomes 1, slave_wait is 0 and the FSM advances rather than waiting; flag any assertion of slave_wait in this non-holding condition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported START command (cmd=0001) on a clk_en-enabled cycle. Model the bus open-drain behavior with scl_i held low by an external participant. Allow synchronization and filtering to establish sscl=0, then wait until the command phase releases SCL, observable as scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: Once scl_oen=1 while sscl=0, slave_wait asserts and remains asserted, indicating that a slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low. The command timing does not advance through the released-high phase until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge, compare the DUT slave_wait probe and command-phase progress against a reference model using the synchronized, filtered SCL value; create bins for scl_oen=1/sscl=0 and slave_wait=1, and assert that no high-phase FSM transition occurs while slave_wait is asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue the same supported START command (cmd=0001) on a clk_en-enabled cycle, but do not hold SCL low externally: drive scl_i high and allow filtering to establish sscl=1 before and after the command releases SCL, observable as scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: When scl_oen=1 and sscl=1, slave_wait remains deasserted; the contrasting non-holding case does not indicate that a slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low, and the command proceeds through its released-high phase.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge, compare slave_wait and command-phase progress with the reference model for sscl=1; create bins for scl_oen=1/sscl=1 and slave_wait=0, and assert that the released-high phase is not blocked by slave_wait.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) on a rising edge. Model the external bus as open drain and hold scl_i=0 continuously, including long enough for the synchronized and majority-filtered SCL value sscl to become 0. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL, keep scl_i=0 for at least four enabled clock opportunities while slave_wait is asserted.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observed behavior: while scl_oen=1, sscl=0, and slave_wait=1, scl_oen remains 1 and the controller does not advance to the SCL-low phase. The timing counter remains paused, clk_en is not generated for FSM progression, and no later WRITE phase occurs until sscl becomes 1.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronization, filter, divider, and slave-wait condition. At settled post-posedge samples, assert that scl_oen stays 1 across the entire filtered-low interval and that the counter value and FSM phase do not advance. Then drive scl_i=1, wait for sscl=1, and check that the next enabled phase changes scl_oen to 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, din=0, and issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) on a rising edge. Keep scl_i=1 so that synchronized and majority-filtered SCL remain high when the WRITE sequence releases SCL; do not introduce clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting, non-holding side of the observed behavior: after SCL is released, slave_wait is not asserted and the timing counter continues. At the next enabled timing phase, scl_oen becomes 0, showing that the controller advances to the SCL-low phase rather than remaining at scl_oen=1.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to predict clk_en and the WRITE phase transitions. At settled post-posedge samples after the release phase, verify sscl=1, slave_wait=0, and that scl_oen changes from 1 to 0 on the first enabled timing phase. Check that this transition occurs without requiring any external SCL release event.

elements.stimulus: Encounter numbered list item 4 during requirements-to-testplan generation; apply no command, reset, clock, or bus stimulus to the DUT.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, and ena high, issue a valid READ command with clk_cnt set to a small nonzero value. Allow the FSM to reach the read_sample_window with scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL high, then have an external participant pull scl_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a falling edge on sscl while scl_oen remains 1.
elements.expected_response: The scl_sync probe asserts when the filtered SCL falling edge is detected while the controller has released SCL high.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer, filter sampling interval, three-sample majority filter, and filtered-edge detection. At each settled posedge, compare the predicted falling-edge event during scl_oen=1 with the scl_sync probe and require an assertion on the predicted detection cycle.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, and ena high, issue a valid READ command with clk_cnt set to a small nonzero value. Allow the FSM to reach the read_sample_window with scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL high, then keep scl_i high without any external falling transition for the entire released-SCL interval.
elements.expected_response: Because no falling edge occurs on filtered SCL while SCL is released, scl_sync remains deasserted throughout the interval; this is the non-occurrence side of the requirement's observable difference.
elements.check_method: Use the same synchronizer and filter reference model to confirm that sscl has no high-to-low transition while scl_oen=1, and assert that scl_sync never asserts during that interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and provide a released-high bus. Issue START and wait for its cmd_ack, then issue READ. During the READ sample window, keep scl_i high while scl_oen is 1 for enough enabled clocks to cover synchronizer and filter settling.
elements.expected_response: The condition for REQ-0059 does not hold because no falling edge occurs on filtered SCL while the controller has released SCL high; scl_sync remains deasserted and no external-master clock-synchronization indication is generated.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen, sscl, and scl_sync after each posedge. Use a reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer and three-sample majority filter to confirm filtered SCL remains high and assert that scl_sync never asserts during the released-high interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and provide a released-high bus. Issue START and wait for its cmd_ack, then issue READ. During the READ sample window, wait until scl_oen is 1 and filtered SCL is high, then have an external master force scl_i low and hold it low long enough for the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample filter to recognize the falling edge.
elements.expected_response: Because the controller has released SCL high and another master forces the shared SCL low, the filtered-SCL falling edge indicates that another master forced SCL low; scl_sync asserts for the detected falling edge.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen, cscl, sscl, and scl_sync after each posedge. Compare against a reference synchronizer/filter model and require scl_sync to assert only after the externally driven low level produces a filtered SCL high-to-low transition while scl_oen remains 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, keep the bus released and high, issue a WRITE command with din=0, and wait until the WRITE sequence releases SCL during its high phase (scl_oen=1). While the command is still active and before its normal completion, force scl_i low externally and hold it low long enough to propagate through synchronization and filtering, then release it high.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SCL falling event while scl_oen=1 causes synchronization of the shared clock: the low-period timing is restarted and command completion is postponed. cmd_ack remains low through the additional reloaded low-period timing and then asserts as exactly one clock pulse only after the restarted timing and the remaining WRITE sequence complete; no earlier completion pulse is permitted.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronization, filter latency, counter reload, and low-period timing. Compare the observed cmd_ack pulse against the predicted postponed completion time and verify it is later than the no-event baseline for the identical WRITE stimulus. Correlate the delay with the scl_sync probe while sampling registered outputs after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, keep the bus released and high, issue the identical WRITE command with din=0, and allow the WRITE sequence to run without any external SCL-low assertion while scl_oen=1; keep scl_i high until command completion.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting no-synchronization-event case: cmd_ack occurs at the normal command-completion timing predicted for the WRITE sequence, as a single one-clock pulse, with no synchronization-induced postponement.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference model and compare the observed cmd_ack cycle with the normal baseline latency. Confirm no scl_sync event occurs before completion and use this result as the timing reference for TP-0000.

elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, input condition, output value, state transition, or timing constraint is required or attributed to REQ-0061.
elements.check_method: Static requirements-to-testplan audit: confirm the quoted obligation contains no behavioral assertion and that no implementation or simulation check is derived from this requirement.

elements.stimulus: After reset, present stable scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 before a rising edge of clk, hold ena=1, and keep both inputs unchanged for at least three consecutive rising edges. Repeat with scl_i=0 and sda_i=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: cscl and csda remain at their prior synchronized values immediately after the first sampling edge, then update to the corresponding stable scl_i and sda_i values only after the two-stage synchronization latency. Subsequent clocks retain the captured values while the raw inputs remain stable; downstream filtering processes cscl/csda rather than the raw inputs.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare cscl and csda against a reference two-stage synchronizer model driven by scl_i and sda_i. Bin the first edge at which each synchronized value changes and assert that the probes do not change earlier than the model's stage-2 output.

elements.stimulus: With the synchronizers initialized and cscl/csda holding known values, change scl_i and sda_i immediately after a rising edge of clk, then observe cscl and csda on the next rising edge before returning the inputs to their original values. Repeat with independent changes on scl_i and sda_i.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: cscl and csda do not immediately mirror the changed raw scl_i and sda_i on the first following clock; they retain the prior synchronized values or the reference model's intermediate-stage result. The changed values become visible only after propagation through the second synchronization stage, demonstrating that external inputs are captured before further processing rather than directly consumed.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate two-stage synchronizer reference model and compare cscl/csda after each settled posedge. Assert no same-cycle or one-stage-early direct reflection of the raw input transition, and assert eventual agreement with the synchronized model after the required pipeline latency.

elements.stimulus: Release both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, then drive stable raw scl_i=0 and sda_i=1 long enough for the two-stage synchronizers to contain those values. Continue enabled clocks through a filter-counter expiration and repeat for several sampling intervals.
elements.expected_response: On each enabled filter-counter expiration, fscl and fsda shift the current synchronized SCL and SDA samples into their respective sample histories, with the history contents and shift order matching the reference model. This is the holding side of the requirement: synchronized samples are shifted when the sampling interval expires.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered updates settle, compare filter_cnt, fscl, and fsda with a cycle-accurate model of the enabled filter counter, two-stage synchronizers, and history shift. Add coverage for multiple consecutive expiration events and verify the histories eventually contain the driven synchronized values.

elements.stimulus: Release both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=1, and observe an enabled clock after the synchronized samples have changed but before the next filter-counter expiration; repeat observations between successive expiration events.
elements.expected_response: While the filter sampling interval has not expired, fscl and fsda do not shift and retain their previous history contents, even though the synchronized cscl and csda values may already differ. This is the non-holding side of the requirement: no synchronized samples are shifted before the filter counter expires.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter-counter model to identify enabled cycles with filter_cnt non-expired, then assert fscl and fsda equal their immediately preceding values on those cycles; separately compare cscl/csda to show that the absence of a history update is due to the sampling interval, not unchanged inputs.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, then drive scl_i and sda_i so that, after the two-stage synchronizers and at three successive filter-counter expirations, the fscl and fsda histories each contain a 2-to-1 majority of 1 (for example, synchronized samples 1, 1, 0). Keep reset inactive and continue enabled long enough for the histories and filtered outputs to update.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed behavior: sscl is 1 whenever the corresponding fscl three-sample history has a majority of 1, and ssda is 1 whenever the corresponding fsda history has a majority of 1, including the 1,1,0 history. The outputs do not follow the minority sample.
elements.check_method: At every filter_cnt expiration after synchronized samples are shifted, record fscl and fsda and compute each three-bit majority as (a & b) | (a & c) | (b & c). Compare the computed majority values with sscl and ssda after registered updates using a cycle-accurate reference model.

elements.stimulus: With nReset released, ena=1, and clk_cnt=4, drive scl_i and sda_i so that, after synchronization and three successive filter-counter expirations, the fscl and fsda histories each contain a 2-to-1 majority of 0 (for example, synchronized samples 0, 0, 1). Keep reset inactive and continue enabled through the sample and output update cycles.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the observed behavior: sscl is 0 whenever the corresponding fscl three-sample history has a majority of 0, and ssda is 0 whenever the corresponding fsda history has a majority of 0, including the 0,0,1 history. The outputs do not follow the minority sample.
elements.check_method: At each filter sampling event, capture the observed fscl and fsda histories, calculate their three-sample majority with (a & b) | (a & c) | (b & c), and compare the result against sscl and ssda after the registered update. Fail if either filtered output differs from its history majority.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16 with scl_i=sda_i=1. Drive scl_i low for one clk period, shorter than the interval needed to produce two sampled low values in the three-sample filter history, then return scl_i high and keep sda_i high.
elements.expected_response: The short SCL glitch is the suppressed side of the requirement: sscl remains high throughout and after the glitch, while ssda remains high; no filtered low transition is produced by the glitch.
elements.check_method: At every filter_cnt expiration, compare the observed fscl history and sscl against a reference model of the two-stage synchronizer, sampling interval floor(clk_cnt/4), three-sample majority, and delayed updates. Assert that the glitch produces no sscl change.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16 with scl_i=sda_i=1. Drive sda_i low for one clk period, shorter than the interval needed to produce two sampled low values in the three-sample filter history, then return sda_i high and keep scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: The short SDA glitch is the suppressed side of the requirement: ssda remains high throughout and after the glitch, while sscl remains high; no filtered low transition is produced by the glitch.
elements.check_method: At every filter_cnt expiration, compare the observed fsda history and ssda against a reference model of the two-stage synchronizer, sampling interval floor(clk_cnt/4), three-sample majority, and delayed updates. Assert that the glitch produces no ssda change.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16 with scl_i=sda_i=1. Drive scl_i low and hold it through at least three filter sampling events, then keep it low for two additional sampling events.
elements.expected_response: The sustained SCL change is the contrasting, non-suppressed side of the requirement: sscl eventually changes to low after the majority history contains sufficient low samples and remains low while scl_i is held low; ssda remains high.
elements.check_method: Use a filter reference model to predict the first enabled sample at which the three-sample majority becomes low. Compare sscl cycle-by-cycle, allowing only the modeled synchronizer and filter latency, and verify persistence while the raw input remains low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16 with scl_i=sda_i=1. Drive sda_i low and hold it through at least three filter sampling events, then keep it low for two additional sampling events.
elements.expected_response: The sustained SDA change is the contrasting, non-suppressed side of the requirement: ssda eventually changes to low after the majority history contains sufficient low samples and remains low while sda_i is held low; sscl remains high.
elements.check_method: Use a filter reference model to predict the first enabled sample at which the three-sample majority becomes low. Compare ssda cycle-by-cycle, allowing only the modeled synchronizer and filter latency, and verify persistence while the raw input remains low.

elements.stimulus: Apply no DUT stimulus; review the source item identified as list item 6 and its associated requirement metadata.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavioral response, interface obligation, command sequence, or status change is required for this item.
elements.check_method: Manual requirements-traceability review confirming the item contains only the statement that no requirement is stated and defines no observable behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Keep the external SCL line high and SDA high for enough enabled clocks to pass synchronization and at least three filter samples; do not introduce any SDA transition.
elements.expected_response: The non-holding side of the requirement is observed: filtered SCL remains high, filtered SDA remains high, and sta_condition remains 0 throughout the interval.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the stable filtered-high interval, then sample sta_condition after each settled posedge and assert it never becomes 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Hold the external SCL line high and SDA high until the synchronized and filtered histories are established, then drive SDA low and hold it low for enough enabled clocks to pass the two-stage synchronizer and at least three filter samples.
elements.expected_response: The holding side of the requirement is observed: when the reference model determines that filtered SDA falls while filtered SCL is high, sta_condition asserts for the corresponding detection interval.
elements.check_method: Predict the filtered SDA transition and delayed filtered SDA value with the reference model; compare sta_condition after settled posedges and require assertion exactly when the predicate ~sSDA & dSDA & sSCL is true, with no assertion before the filtered falling edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the external bus released and drive scl_i high. Drive sda_i low long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to settle low, then drive sda_i high and hold it long enough for the filtered SDA to transition from low to high while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sto_condition asserts when the filtered SDA rising transition is observed with filtered SCL high, indicating that an I2C STOP condition has been detected.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, majority filtering, and delayed filtered SDA. Compare the modeled STOP predicate (ssda=1, prior delayed SDA=0, sscl=1) with the sto_condition probe on every clock, requiring assertion on the modeled qualifying cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep scl_i high and drive sda_i low long enough for filtered SDA to settle low, then either keep sda_i low for the observation window or make sda_i rise only while scl_i is low; allow synchronization and filtering to settle after each change.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: sto_condition remains deasserted; no STOP detection is reported when filtered SDA does not rise while filtered SCL is high.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate synchronizer/filter reference model to identify all cycles lacking the qualifying filtered SDA rising edge with filtered SCL high, and assert that sto_condition is 0 on those cycles.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0, then release it; keep rst=0 and ena=1. With the filtered bus initially high, hold scl_i=1 and drive sda_i from 1 to 0, maintaining the levels long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to assert sta_condition. After START detection, keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 without producing a filtered STOP.
elements.expected_response: The busy output is low before the filtered START, becomes high when the START condition is detected, and remains high throughout the interval after START detection while no STOP condition is detected. This is the high/holding side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter and edge-detection model to identify the cycle where sta_condition asserts; compare registered busy cycle-by-cycle, requiring busy=1 from the post-START observation through every subsequent sampled cycle before any STOP.

elements.stimulus: Reset and release the DUT with rst=0 and ena=1. With scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, first drive sda_i low while scl_i remains high long enough to produce a filtered START and establish busy=1. Then, after a stable low filtered SDA interval, drive sda_i high while keeping scl_i=1 long enough to produce a filtered STOP; hold both lines high afterward.
elements.expected_response: busy is high between the detected filtered START and filtered STOP, becomes low when the STOP condition is detected, and remains low during the post-STOP idle interval. This is the cleared/post-STOP side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Align observations to the reference model's filtered sta_condition and sto_condition cycles, then compare the registered busy output: require high in the START-to-STOP interval and low on the STOP-processing cycle and all subsequent post-STOP cycles.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset so al is low. With ena=1, issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1. During the stable-high WRITE phase, wait until sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, then externally drive SDA low long enough for the synchronized and majority-filtered ssda to become 0 while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: The arbitration-loss condition holds and al asserts; this is the asserting side of the observed al behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after ssda=0 is established during sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, compare the registered al output against an assertion that it becomes 1. Also verify al remains 1 after the command aborts until reset.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset so al is low. With ena=1, issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1. During the stable-high WRITE phase, wait until sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, and allow the external bus to remain high long enough for the synchronized and majority-filtered ssda to remain 1.
elements.expected_response: The arbitration-loss condition does not hold and al remains unasserted throughout the arbitration-checking phase; this is the non-asserting side of the observed al behavior.
elements.check_method: While sda_chk=1, sda_oen=1, and ssda=1, sample al after each posedge and compare it with the expected value 0; ensure no arbitration-loss abort or al assertion occurs before normal WRITE completion.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command, and wait until the command FSM is active. While the command is active and scl_i is released high, drive an external SDA transition from low to high and hold scl_i and sda_i high long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to produce a filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case: when sto_condition is detected while active_command is asserted and the current command is not STOP, al asserts on the registered cycle that processes the filtered STOP condition. The active command aborts and both output enables are released; cmd_ack is not generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use the sto_condition and active_command probes to identify the filtered STOP-detection cycle, then sample al after the corresponding posedge and compare against a reference model. Also verify no cmd_ack pulse follows the aborted command and that scl_oen and sda_oen are released.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 with the bus released high, issue a STOP command, and allow the complete requested STOP sequence to execute, including the filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case: although sto_condition is detected during the requested STOP sequence, al does not assert in response to this STOP condition. The STOP command completes normally and generates its one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the stop_sequence and sto_condition probes to identify the requested STOP detection and terminal phase, then check after each relevant posedge that al remains low and that exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs at normal command completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena=1 and a released-high bus; after START completes, issue WRITE with cmd=0100 and din=1. During the WRITE stable-high arbitration-check phase, keep sda_oen released and externally drive SDA low long enough for filtered ssda to become 0 while SCL is released high.
elements.expected_response: Arbitration loss is indicated by registered al=1. On the arbitration-loss handling cycle or immediately following registered state update, the command FSM is idle and both scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, releasing SCL and SDA. No cmd_ack is generated for the aborted WRITE.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after NBA settling, correlate al with the idle probe and compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the reference FSM model. Assert that al becomes high, idle is reached, both output enables are high, and cmd_ack remains low for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, START, and WRITE cmd=0100, din=1 sequence, but keep the external SDA line high during the released-high WRITE arbitration-check phase so filtered ssda remains 1.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ordinary case: al remains 0, the FSM does not return to idle due to arbitration loss, and scl_oen and sda_oen follow the normal WRITE timing rather than being forced high by arbitration-loss handling. The WRITE proceeds to its normal completion and cmd_ack is asserted once.
elements.check_method: During the WRITE stable-high phase and the following enabled phases, compare al, idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen with the normal WRITE reference-model trace; verify no arbitration-loss transition occurs and that the command reaches normal acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: Apply the normal reset and idle stimulus sequence: assert nReset low between clock edges, release it, then hold rst low, ena high, cmd=NOP, and both external bus inputs high for at least four rising edges. Evaluate this trace with list-item marker 9 considered present.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: because REQ-0073 states that list-item marker 9 has no hardware obligation, no REQ-0073-specific output, state transition, timing change, or interface response is required. The observed DUT trace is accepted without any additional behavior attributed to REQ-0073.
elements.check_method: Run the baseline trace and apply no REQ-0073-specific assertions; confirm that the checker records the holding case as unconstrained rather than requiring a special output response.

elements.stimulus: Repeat exactly the same reset, release, idle, and NOP stimulus sequence as TP-0000, but evaluate the trace with list-item marker 9 considered absent or not applicable.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because REQ-0073 states that list-item marker 9 has no hardware obligation, the DUT must have no observable behavior that differs specifically due to this marker being absent. No REQ-0073-specific output, state transition, timing change, or interface response is required.
elements.check_method: Compare all sampled DUT outputs and available probes from this trace against TP-0000 under identical initial conditions; require no marker-dependent difference and do not impose any additional functional expectation.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold the external bus with scl_i=0 and sda_i=1 long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce filtered SCL low and filtered SDA high, then issue cmd=READ (1000). After the command reaches the READ sample window and scl_oen is released, drive scl_i high and hold sda_i=1 long enough for a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the filtered SCL rising edge while read_sample_window is active, dout updates to the filtered SDA value 1 on the registered sampling update; the READ sequence then pulls SCL low and eventually produces its command-complete pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter histories, majority-filtered SCL/SDA, READ phase, and filtered rising-edge detection. At each settled posedge, compare dout with the model and require exactly one update to 1 at the sampled filtered SCL rising edge, with no earlier update caused by raw inputs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, perform an enabled READ with clk_cnt=0 and establish sda_i=1 so dout becomes 1 at a valid filtered SCL rising edge in the READ sample window. Allow the READ phase to pull SCL low and leave the sample window, then keep scl_oen=0 and drive the external scl_i high, holding it long enough to create a filtered SCL rising edge while the controller is not in read_sample_window.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: at the filtered SCL rising edge outside the READ sample window, dout does not update to the filtered SDA value; it retains the previously captured value 1. No additional READ data capture is permitted.
elements.check_method: Track read_sample_window and filtered SCL edges in a cycle-accurate reference model. Compare dout before and after the outside-window filtered rising edge and require it to remain unchanged, while separately confirming that the preceding in-window sample captured 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while idle. Wait for the READ sampling window in which SDA is released and SCL is released high. Drive the external bus so filtered SDA is 0, then produce one filtered SCL low-to-high edge and hold filtered SDA stable through that edge.
elements.expected_response: At the registered cycle processing the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 0 and presents that value as the received data bit for collection by the byte-level controller; this is the side of the requirement's shows clause where dout captures and presents the filtered SDA value.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge and filtered SDA value, then compare the post-posedge dout value with the modeled SDA value and verify the update occurs only at that sampling event.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while idle. Enter the READ sampling window, release SDA, drive the external bus so filtered SDA is 1, and produce one filtered SCL low-to-high edge while holding filtered SDA stable high.
elements.expected_response: At the registered cycle processing the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 1 and presents that value as the received data bit for collection by the byte-level controller; this is the side of the requirement's shows clause where dout captures and presents the filtered SDA value.
elements.check_method: Model synchronization and majority filtering to determine the filtered SCL rising edge and filtered SDA=1, then compare dout immediately after the corresponding posedge against 1 and verify the capture is associated with that edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) while idle. Enter the READ sampling window with SDA released. Change the external SDA input, but keep filtered SCL low and do not allow any filtered SCL low-to-high edge during the observation interval.
elements.expected_response: dout does not update to a newly captured received data bit during the interval because the required filtered SCL rising-edge sampling event did not occur; this is the otherwise side of the requirement's shows clause.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm no filtered SCL rising edge occurred, then compare dout before and after the interval and assert that it remains unchanged, with no new capture event observed.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue a START command while idle, and continue clocking until the active START sequence reaches successive timing-phase boundaries. Record clk_en and scl_oen after each posedge.
elements.expected_response: This is the clk_en-asserted side of the requirement: whenever clk_en=1 at a phase boundary during the active START sequence, the command FSM advances to the next timing phase and scl_oen changes as required by that phase; no phase advancement is deferred when the timing-enable tick is present.
elements.check_method: Use the clk_en probe as the reference-model timing tick and compare the observed scl_oen sequence against the START phase model. Assert that every expected phase-changing scl_oen transition occurs only on a posedge with clk_en=1 and that the phase index advances exactly once per such tick.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue a START command while idle, and while the START sequence is active monitor clock edges for cycles where clk_en=0 between timing ticks.
elements.expected_response: This is the clk_en-not-asserted side of the requirement: on every posedge with clk_en=0, the command FSM remains in its current timing phase and scl_oen holds its previous phase value; a phase-changing scl_oen transition on such an edge is forbidden.
elements.check_method: At each posedge with clk_en=0, compare scl_oen and the reference-model phase against their values from the preceding posedge. Require no scl_oen transition and no phase advancement, while allowing advancement on the next posedge where clk_en=1.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, then drive cmd=4'b0001 (START) before the next enabled posedge.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled command-acceptance tick, the FSM enters the START sequence; start_sequence becomes asserted and the other command-sequence probes remain deasserted. This is the supported-command holding case for START.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset values settle, compare start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence against a reference FSM keyed by cmd and clk_en; require START entry on the acceptance tick.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, then drive cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) before the next enabled posedge.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled command-acceptance tick, the FSM enters the STOP sequence; stop_sequence becomes asserted and the other command-sequence probes remain deasserted. This is the supported-command holding case for STOP.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset values settle, compare stop_sequence, start_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence against a reference FSM keyed by cmd and clk_en; require STOP entry on the acceptance tick.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, then drive cmd=4'b1000 (READ) before the next enabled posedge.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled command-acceptance tick, the FSM enters the READ sequence; read_sequence becomes asserted and the other command-sequence probes remain deasserted. This is the supported-command holding case for READ.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset values settle, compare read_sequence, start_sequence, stop_sequence, and write_sequence against a reference FSM keyed by cmd and clk_en; require READ entry on the acceptance tick.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, then drive cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) before the next enabled posedge.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled command-acceptance tick, the FSM enters the WRITE sequence; write_sequence becomes asserted and the other command-sequence probes remain deasserted. This is the supported-command holding case for WRITE.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset values settle, compare write_sequence, start_sequence, stop_sequence, and read_sequence against a reference FSM keyed by cmd and clk_en; require WRITE entry on the acceptance tick.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, wait until idle=1 and clk_en=1, then drive an unsupported cmd value such as cmd=4'b0011 before the next enabled posedge.
elements.expected_response: At the enabled idle tick, no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE sequence is entered; idle remains asserted and all four command-sequence probes remain deasserted. This is the contrasting non-holding case: no supported command is decoded, so no corresponding sequence exists.
elements.check_method: Sample idle and all four sequence probes after the enabled posedge and compare with the reference model; require no sequence-entry transition for the unsupported encoding.
