elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=START=4'b0001 from idle. On each clk_en tick, continue providing a released-high bus until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the active START sequence, scl_oen and sda_oen follow the START timing phases: both are released (1,1), SDA is driven low while SCL remains released (scl_oen=1, sda_oen=0), and then both lines are driven low (0,0). sda_chk remains deasserted. The sequence ends with one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a phase-aware scoreboard keyed to start_sequence and clk_en; compare sampled scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk after each posedge against the prescribed START phase values and verify exactly one terminal cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=STOP=4'b0010 from idle. Keep the bus released as required and wait for cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the active STOP sequence, SDA is first driven low, SCL is then released while SDA remains driven low, and finally SDA is released while SCL is high: the observed enable phases include (scl_oen,sda_oen)=(0,0), then (1,0), then (1,1). sda_chk remains deasserted. This is the prescribed-value, or shows, side of the port observation.
elements.check_method: Use stop_sequence and clk_en probes to identify each STOP phase and compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the ordered expected enable tuple; check that no phase uses the other command's enable pattern and that cmd_ack is one clock.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, hold sda_i=1, issue cmd=READ=4'b1000, and allow scl_i to remain high so the read window can execute. Wait for the read sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: During READ, SDA remains released throughout (sda_oen=1); SCL is initially driven low and is released for the read sample window (scl_oen=1), then is driven low again (scl_oen=0). sda_chk remains deasserted. The sequence ends with one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use read_sequence and read_sample_window probes to delimit the phases; compare sda_oen and scl_oen at every clk_en transition with the READ timing model and verify sda_chk=0 and a single cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, drive din=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100. Allow the complete write bit sequence to execute.
elements.expected_response: During WRITE with din=0, SDA is driven low before and during the data bit, SCL is released for the high phase and then driven low, and sda_chk is asserted only during the stable released-SCL-high write phase. Thus the data phases include sda_oen=0, followed by scl_oen=1 with sda_oen=0 and sda_chk=1, followed by scl_oen=0. No arbitration loss occurs and one cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Use write_sequence, write_stable_high_phase, and clk_en probes to compare scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk against the din=0 WRITE phase model; assert al remains low and count cmd_ack pulses.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, drive din=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 so arbitration succeeds, then issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100 and wait for completion.
elements.expected_response: During WRITE with din=1, SDA is released for the data bit (sda_oen=1), SCL is released for the high phase and then driven low, and sda_chk is asserted during the stable released-SCL-high phase. The required phases include scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, sda_chk=1 during the high phase, followed by scl_oen=0. No arbitration loss occurs and one cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Use write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase probes to compare all clk_en-driven output-enable and sda_chk values with the din=1 WRITE model, and verify al=0 plus exactly one cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Run two isolated enabled transactions with clk_cnt=1 and a released-high bus: first issue START and observe its SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase; after reset, issue READ and observe its released-SDA read window. In both runs sample outputs after each clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: The port behavior must differ according to the active sequence, not merely show generic clock activity. In the START SDA-low phase, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=0; in the READ sample window, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1. The START and READ sda_chk values remain 0. The START and READ cases are both on the prescribed-value, or shows, side of the observation; a checker must flag either phase if it instead holds the other command's value.
elements.check_method: Correlate start_sequence and read_sample_window with clk_en and use a differential scoreboard to compare the command-specific output-enable tuples at the otherwise similar SCL-released phases; flag any missing command-specific difference.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, hold cmd=START while the FSM is idle until an enabled timing tick accepts it, and provide a released-high bus so the START sequence can complete.
elements.expected_response: At START sequence completion, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock cycle; this is the positive side of the observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare idle and cmd_ack against a command-sequence reference model; assert that the completion transition has idle=1 and cmd_ack=1, with cmd_ack=0 on the immediately preceding and following clocks.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, hold cmd=STOP while the FSM is idle until an enabled timing tick accepts it, and provide bus conditions that allow the STOP sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: At STOP sequence completion, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock cycle; this is the positive side of the observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify the STOP terminal phase and compare registered idle and cmd_ack at each posedge; require one and only one cmd_ack cycle coincident with return to idle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, hold cmd=READ while the FSM is idle until acceptance, and provide a responding bus with SCL and SDA transitions that allow the READ bit sequence to reach its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: When the READ sequence completes, the FSM is idle and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle, regardless of the variable sequence latency; this is the positive side of the observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: Track the modeled READ phases rather than assuming a fixed latency, then assert that cmd_ack is a one-cycle registered pulse at terminal completion and is low throughout all earlier and later cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, drive din=1, and hold cmd=WRITE while the FSM is idle until acceptance; keep the external bus released and high so the WRITE sequence completes without interruption.
elements.expected_response: At WRITE sequence completion, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle; this is the positive side of the observed_via shows clause.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed terminal phase, idle, and cmd_ack with a bit-level WRITE reference model and assert the pulse width is exactly one clk period with no duplicate or delayed ack.

elements.stimulus: Accept a WRITE command with ena high, then assert synchronous rst on a posedge while the command is still in progress, before its terminal completion phase.
elements.expected_response: Because the command does not reach completion, cmd_ack remains absent and the reset returns the FSM to idle; this is the contrasting otherwise side of the observed_via shows clause, not a completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Assert that no cmd_ack pulse occurs on the reset edge or any subsequent clock until a new command is accepted, and sample idle high after the reset update.

elements.stimulus: With the DUT reset and idle, treat the specification item as holding because it is labeled item 11. Drive ena=1, cmd=0000 (NOP), and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for several rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: the item label 11 produces no DUT behavior. The ordinary idle NOP behavior is observed: cmd_ack remains low, busy remains low, al remains low, and both scl_oen and sda_oen remain released high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare cmd_ack, busy, al, scl_oen, and sda_oen against the idle-NOP reference model; additionally check that no output changes are attributable to the documentation label.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset-to-idle sequence with ena=1, cmd=0000 (NOP), scl_i=1, and sda_i=1, but treat the specification item as not holding because its label is changed or absent.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding side of the requirement: absence of the item label also produces no DUT behavior. The same ordinary idle NOP behavior is observed: cmd_ack remains low, busy remains low, al remains low, and both scl_oen and sda_oen remain released high.
elements.check_method: Compare all observed outputs cycle-by-cycle with TP-0000 and the idle-NOP reference model; pass only if the holding and non-holding cases are indistinguishable at the DUT ports.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus externally released high, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b0001 (START), and hold these inputs until cmd_ack is observed. Use a nonzero clk_cnt and allow every required clk_en timing tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the START command is accepted. The output enables first show scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 (both lines released), then show scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=0 (SDA pulled low while SCL remains high), then show scl_oen=0 (SCL pulled low). At the terminal phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock and the START sequence returns to idle.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare the observed scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack trace against a reference START-sequence model keyed to clk_en. Assert the required phase ordering, require cmd_ack only after the SDA-low/SCL-high phase followed by SCL-low, and assert that cmd_ack is a one-clock pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set cmd=4'b0001 (START) while ena=0, keep the external bus released high, and hold ena low for multiple clk_en intervals before optionally changing cmd to NOP.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the enabled-START condition does not hold, so cmd_ack remains low, no START terminal phase occurs, and the controller does not execute the SDA-low-while-SCL-high followed by SCL-low sequence; both output enables remain released while ena is low.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack after every posedge for the entire ena-low interval. Assert no cmd_ack pulse and no transition to the START output-enable sequence; use the idle/enable reference model to distinguish this non-holding case from the enabled START trace.

elements.stimulus: Run the DUT through a representative reset followed by a legal command sequence while marking specification item 12 as considered in the requirement-traceability input.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: no hardware output behavior is required or attributed to item 12; cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, and output enables may follow the behavior of other applicable requirements, with no additional item-12-specific constraint.
elements.check_method: Traceability checker confirms REQ-0082@1 has no hardware-owned port, activation condition, observable, or DUT assertion, and that the scenario produces no item-12-specific comparison failure.

elements.stimulus: Run the DUT through the same representative reset and legal command sequence without considering specification item 12 in the requirement-traceability input.
elements.expected_response: Not-holding side of shows: the DUT has no required change at any port because item 12 specifies no hardware behavior; all observed outputs remain governed only by other applicable requirements.
elements.check_method: Compare the traceability and DUT-observation results against the item-12-considered run; verify no item-12-specific output obligation or difference is reported and no unrelated requirement check is attributed to REQ-0082@1.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=0010 (STOP) while idle. Keep the command and released-high bus applied until the STOP command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0083: during stop_sequence, sda_oen first drives SDA low while scl_oen remains low, then scl_oen releases high before sda_oen releases high, and scl_oen remains high through the final SDA release. The resulting output-enable order is SDA drive-low, SCL release, SDA release, creating a STOP condition.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after registered outputs settle, collect the scl_oen and sda_oen trace while stop_sequence is asserted. Use a temporal checker requiring the ordered phases sda_oen=0 before scl_oen=1, then scl_oen=1 before sda_oen=1, with scl_oen remaining 1 until and through the sda_oen=1 phase; fail if SDA releases before SCL or if SCL is reasserted during final SDA release.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=0000 (NOP) while idle. Hold cmd=0000 for at least eight enabled clocks and do not issue a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0083: the STOP-specific behavior must not occur. scl_oen and sda_oen remain in their released idle pair (1,1), so there is no SDA-low phase followed by SCL release and final SDA release; specifically, the STOP ordering described by the requirement is absent.
elements.check_method: Trace scl_oen and sda_oen over the NOP interval and assert that no subsequence matching the STOP signature occurs: no sda_oen=0 phase followed by scl_oen=1 and then sda_oen=1. Also verify both enables remain 1 throughout the interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1 and drive a released-high bus. Present cmd=0010 (STOP) while idle and hold it through the enabled command-acceptance tick. Allow the STOP sequence to progress through sda_oen=0 with SCL released, then scl_oen=1, and finally sda_oen=1 while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: This is the requirement-holds case: after SDA has been released high while SCL is high, cmd_ack asserts on the following clock edge as a one-clock pulse. No earlier cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor the registered output enables and filtered SCL to identify the terminal STOP phase, then compare cmd_ack at the immediately following posedge against a reference STOP-sequence model; assert exactly one high cycle and no high cycle before terminal-phase completion.

elements.stimulus: After accepting cmd=0010 with ena=1, allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low but assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the sequence releases SDA high while SCL is high; deassert nReset and continue clocking without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting requirement-does-not-hold case: the STOP terminal phase is aborted, so cmd_ack remains deasserted during and after the would-have-been completion window; reset leaves the controller idle with both output enables released.
elements.check_method: Use a reset-aware reference model to mark the STOP command aborted before terminal completion, sample cmd_ack after reset release and across the expected terminal window, and assert that no cmd_ack pulse occurs for the aborted command while checking idle=1, sda_oen=1, and scl_oen=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while the bus is released high. Allow the READ sequence to reach its data-bit sample window, keep the external SCL high for sampling, and hold the transaction active until before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit sample window, sda_oen is high, which is the 'shows' side of the requirement: SDA is released so the slave can drive the data bit.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from read_sequence activation through the sample window and until cmd_ack, assert sda_oen==1; correlate the interval with the READ command sequence and record a coverage bin for the release window.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=0 while the bus is released high. Allow the WRITE sequence to reach its data-bit drive phase before command completion.
elements.expected_response: Outside the READ data-bit sample window, during the WRITE data-bit drive phase, sda_oen is low, which is the 'otherwise' side of the requirement: SDA is driven rather than released.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge during the WRITE data-bit phase before cmd_ack, assert sda_oen==0 and confirm read_sequence is inactive; record a contrasting coverage bin for the non-READ drive behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=READ (4'b1000), clk_cnt=16'd1, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Apply the READ command while idle and continue clocking until the read_sample_window probe asserts; do not assert rst, nReset, or induce arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of observed_via.shows: during read_sample_window, scl_oen becomes 1, releasing SCL high, and remains 1 for the sample window; when the window ends, scl_oen becomes 0, driving SCL low again.
elements.check_method: Monitor read_sample_window and scl_oen after each settled posedge. Assert that every reached READ sample window has an interval with read_sample_window=1 and scl_oen=1, followed by a transition to scl_oen=0 before the READ command completes; fail if the high-release phase or subsequent low-drive phase is missing.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=READ (4'b1000), clk_cnt=16'd1, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Accept the READ command from idle, then assert synchronous rst=1 on a posedge before read_sample_window asserts; deassert rst on the next posedge and leave cmd=NOP.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side of observed_via.shows: because the READ is reset before its sample window, the DUT must not present a READ sample-window sequence on scl_oen; no interval with read_sample_window=1 and scl_oen=1 followed by scl_oen=0 may be attributed to that aborted command.
elements.check_method: Record the read_sample_window probe and scl_oen from READ acceptance through reset recovery. Verify that read_sample_window is never asserted for the aborted command and that no required release-high-then-drive-low sequence occurs in that interval; also verify reset returns scl_oen to its released state.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue the READ command while the bus is idle, hold filtered SDA at 0, and allow the READ sequence to release SCL so that three consecutive synchronized/filter samples produce a rising edge on filtered SCL during the READ sampling window. Repeat with filtered SDA held at 1.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case side of shows: on each filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sampling window, dout updates to the corresponding filtered SDA value, producing dout=0 for the first run and dout=1 for the second run.
elements.check_method: Use the sscl, ssda, and read_sample_window probes to identify each qualifying filtered SCL rising edge; sample dout after the following posedge clk and compare it with ssda at the detected edge using a reference model of synchronization, filtering, and registered dout latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a START command followed by a STOP or otherwise observe a stable filtered SCL rising edge while the command FSM is idle or executing a non-READ sequence; hold filtered SDA at a value different from the current dout and ensure read_sample_window is deasserted at that edge.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding-case side of shows: dout does not update to the filtered SDA value for the filtered SCL rising edge because the edge is outside the READ sampling window; dout retains its prior registered value.
elements.check_method: Use sscl and read_sample_window probes to identify a filtered SCL rising edge with read_sample_window=0, then compare dout before and after the registered update against the expected hold value and verify it does not equal the unrelated filtered SDA transition solely because of that edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while the bus is released high. Provide a valid external read bit on SDA, allow the filtered SCL rising edge to occur and capture the bit, then allow the READ sequence to complete its SCL-low terminal phase. Keep cmd stable until completion and monitor cmd_ack on each posedge.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: after the READ bit cycle has completed, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock to indicate that the READ command has ended, then returns low and does not reassert for the same command.
elements.check_method: Scoreboard the READ sequence and filtered SCL rising edge, then compare the registered cmd_ack waveform: require one and only one high cycle after the terminal READ phase, with no additional pulse before a subsequent command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000). Begin a valid READ operation, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the READ reaches its terminal completion phase; release nReset and provide clock edges afterward without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: cmd_ack does not assert for the aborted READ command during or after the reset interruption; reset returns the controller to its initialized idle state, and any later cmd_ack must not be attributed to the aborted READ.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack from reset assertion through several post-reset clocks and correlate it with the command transaction; require cmd_ack to remain low for the aborted READ and verify that no pulse occurs unless a new READ is subsequently issued and completed.

elements.stimulus: Process numbered list item 14 ('14.') in the requirement-to-testplan traceability review; apply no DUT stimulus.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output, state transition, or test stimulus is required or attributed to item 14.
elements.check_method: Static traceability review confirms the item contains no requirement text, ports, observable outputs, activation conditions, or expected response, and that no executable DUT test is generated from it.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the bus released/high. Set din=0 and present cmd=0100 (WRITE) while the command FSM is idle; hold the command until an enabled timing tick accepts it. Keep the external SCL high and allow the WRITE bit phase to proceed without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: For the din=0 side of the requirement, sda_oen is 0 during the WRITE data-setting phase and remains driven low as SCL is released high for the WRITE high phase. sda_oen therefore matches the required low-drive behavior for din=0.
elements.check_method: At every registered phase transition after WRITE acceptance, assert sda_oen==0 while din=0 during data-setting and the following high phase; correlate the sampled output with the WRITE sequence probe and fail if sda_oen is 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the bus released/high. Set din=1 and present cmd=0100 (WRITE) while the command FSM is idle; hold the command until an enabled timing tick accepts it. Keep external SDA and SCL high, and allow the WRITE bit phase to proceed without reset, stretching, or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: For the din=1 side of the requirement, sda_oen is 1 during the WRITE data-setting phase, releasing SDA. During the subsequent WRITE high phase scl_oen is 1, and it then becomes 0 for the following SCL-low phase. The observed scl_oen ordering is release-high followed by pull-low.
elements.check_method: Use a waveform assertion triggered by WRITE acceptance: verify sda_oen==1 during data-setting and the high phase, verify scl_oen transitions 0->1 after SDA is set and then 1->0 on the next low phase, with no reordering. Correlate phase boundaries with the write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase probes.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set din=0, and issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100 while idle. Keep ena asserted and allow the WRITE sequence to progress through its SDA setup, released-SCL high phase, and terminal SCL-low phase without changing the external bus or asserting reset.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the WRITE sequence reaches its terminal completion phase and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock, then returns low with no additional completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model keyed to clk_en and filtered SCL progression to identify the terminal WRITE phase; compare cmd_ack after each settled posedge and assert that it is high on the terminal completion clock and low on the immediately following clock.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100 while idle. During the WRITE stable SCL-high phase, externally force SDA low while the DUT has released SDA; keep the forced-low condition long enough for filtered arbitration loss to be detected, then observe the command abort before its terminal completion phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because the WRITE is aborted by arbitration loss before completion, al asserts and both output enables are released, while cmd_ack does not pulse high at the aborted command's would-be terminal phase.
elements.check_method: Monitor write_stable_high_phase and sda_chk to confirm the injection occurs in the arbitration window; compare filtered SDA and al against the reference model, and assert that no cmd_ack high pulse occurs from command acceptance through return to idle after arbitration loss.

elements.stimulus: Do not apply any requirement-specific stimulus; treat numbered list item 15 as having no behavioral content.
elements.expected_response: No DUT output behavior is required or inferred from this item.
elements.check_method: Review the test specification and confirm that no behavioral assertion, coverage point, or expected-output comparison is generated for item 15.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset=1 and rst=0, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=sda_i=1, and issue a START command from idle. On an enabled clock, wait until the START sequence is active and its SDA-low/SCL-high phase is observable.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-reset side of the observed-port difference: during ordinary command execution, scl_oen and sda_oen reflect command-phase control rather than reset release; specifically, during the START SDA-low/SCL-high phase, scl_oen is high and sda_oen is low. The FSM is not idle and cmd_ack remains low until command completion.
elements.check_method: Use assertions sampled after each posedge and a reference FSM model to identify the START phase; compare scl_oen, sda_oen, idle, and cmd_ack against the modeled ordinary behavior and ensure the reset values are not required while reset is inactive.

elements.stimulus: Starting from the active START phase established in TP-0000, assert nReset=0 between two rising edges while keeping rst=0. Do not provide a clock edge during the assertion, then observe outputs immediately and through the next clock; deassert nReset only after reset values have been checked.
elements.expected_response: This is the reset side of the observed-port difference: asynchronous reset immediately returns the FSM to idle, drives scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, clears cmd_ack=0, al=0, and busy=0, and resets the timing/filter state with cnt_zero asserted, filter_cnt reset, and sscl=ssda=1. No command-phase output remains active.
elements.check_method: Use immediate asynchronous assertions at the nReset falling edge for the output and probe values, followed by posedge assertions confirming they remain held. Compare all values with a reset reference model and verify no cmd_ack pulse is generated from the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, start a command and wait until the START sequence is active. Assert rst=1 while the clock is running, keep rst high across one rising edge, and then deassert rst after observing the post-edge state.
elements.expected_response: This is the reset side of the observed-port difference for synchronous reset: before the rising edge, ordinary command-phase behavior remains visible; on the first rising edge with rst=1, the FSM becomes idle, scl_oen and sda_oen become high, cmd_ack, al, and busy become low, cnt_zero and filter_cnt indicate reset counter state, and sscl and ssda are high. The reset values are applied synchronously on that edge.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs and probes immediately before and after the rst-qualified rising edge. Assert that no reset transition occurs before the edge, then compare the post-edge state against the reset reference model and verify the command is abandoned without acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: Inspect the i2c_master_bit_ctrl specification text around the documented processing-flow section.
elements.expected_response: The specification contains a section titled exactly "Processing Flow:" identifying the module's processing flow.
elements.check_method: Perform a case-sensitive textual search and assert that exactly the required section heading is present in the specification.

elements.stimulus: While clk is running and the controller is not being reset, assert nReset=0 asynchronously between clock edges; hold it low across a clock edge, then deassert nReset=1 without asserting rst.
elements.expected_response: At asynchronous reset assertion and throughout reset initialization, scl_oen is 1, which is the reset-initialized idle state with SCL released. This is the reset-holding side of the specified observation.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen immediately after nReset assertion and after reset state settles, including before and after the next posedge; compare against a reference reset model requiring scl_oen==1.

elements.stimulus: After releasing reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and hold the external scl_i and sda_i lines high; drive clocks until the START command advances through its sequence to the phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Outside the reset-initialization window, scl_oen follows active command timing and becomes 0 during the START phase that drives SCL low. This is the contrasting, non-reset side of the specified observation.
elements.check_method: Use the command-sequence reference model and sample scl_oen after each posedge; verify it transitions from the reset value 1 to 0 only after command processing begins and while the START sequence is in its SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: Start with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, nReset=1, rst=0, and released-high external SCL/SDA. Issue START and wait until an active START phase is visible, then assert nReset=0 between clk rising edges.
elements.expected_response: As soon as asynchronous nReset is asserted, the module returns to the known idle interface state: cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. This is the reset side of each observed port's behavior.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous assertion monitor to sample outputs immediately after nReset falls, independently of clk; compare all five outputs against the required reset values and verify they remain at those values until reset is released.

elements.stimulus: Start with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, nReset=1, rst=0, and released-high external SCL/SDA. Issue START and wait until an active START phase is visible, then drive rst=1 across a rising edge of clk while leaving nReset=1.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge sampling rst=1, the module returns to the known idle interface state: cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. This is the reset side of each observed port's behavior for synchronous reset.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs after nonblocking assignments settle on the rst-high rising edge and compare them with the reset reference model; verify the values are not required to change before that edge.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset=1 and rst=0, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep external SCL/SDA released high, issue START, and wait for the START sequence to enter its phase that pulls SDA low while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: Because neither reset is asserted, ordinary active-command behavior is allowed instead of the reset state: during the START sequence sda_oen=0 while scl_oen remains released high; cmd_ack, busy, and al may reflect command-progress or bus-status behavior rather than all being forced low. This is the non-reset side of the observed port differences.
elements.check_method: Use the active START phase as the binning event and compare registered output enables after each clk edge against the command reference model, specifically requiring sda_oen=0 and scl_oen=1 in the SDA-low/SCL-high phase; verify no reset-value assertion is expected in this active phase.

elements.stimulus: Start a command with ena=1 and a released-high bus, then assert nReset=0 between clk rising edges while the command is active. Hold nReset low long enough to sample asynchronous outputs, then deassert it without asserting rst.
elements.expected_response: Immediately on asynchronous nReset assertion, the command FSM enters idle, cmd_ack, busy, and al are 0, scl_oen and sda_oen are 1, arbitration checking sda_chk is disabled, and the counters and filter state enter their reset-defined values: timing counters are reset or reloaded as specified and fscl, fsda, sscl, and ssda are initialized high. The active command is aborted and no completion pulse is generated solely because of reset.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous monitor for cmd_ack, busy, al, scl_oen, and sda_oen at nReset assertion, then sample idle, sda_chk, cnt_zero, filter_cnt, fscl, fsda, sscl, and ssda after reset-state settling. Compare all values and counter behavior against a reset-aware reference model and assert that cmd_ack remains low while reset is held.

elements.stimulus: Run a command far enough to make the controller active and, if possible, set busy or al, then assert rst=1 synchronously before a rising edge while nReset remains high. Keep rst high through that rising edge and then deassert rst.
elements.expected_response: At the rising edge sampling rst=1, the command FSM is idle, cmd_ack, busy, and al are cleared to 0, scl_oen and sda_oen are released high at 1, arbitration checking sda_chk is disabled, counters enter their reset or reload state, and fscl, fsda, sscl, and ssda are initialized high. The reset takes effect on that clock edge, not before it, and no command-completion acknowledgement is emitted for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs immediately before and after the rst sampling edge to verify synchronous timing, then compare idle, cmd_ack, busy, al, scl_oen, sda_oen, sda_chk, cnt_zero, filter_cnt, fscl, fsda, sscl, and ssda with the reset-aware reference model. Check that all status and command state remain reset while rst is asserted.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1 and rst=0, leave the controller idle, set ena=1 and cmd=START, and provide a released-high bus. Wait for the enabled timing tick and advance until the START sequence reaches its SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase.
elements.expected_response: Because neither reset is asserted, the ordinary command behavior applies rather than the reset behavior: the FSM leaves idle for the START sequence and sda_oen becomes 0 during the SDA-low phase (while scl_oen remains released as required by that phase), so the reset-side statement that sda_oen is released high is not present. cmd_ack is not asserted until the START sequence terminal phase.
elements.check_method: Observe the start_sequence and idle probes and compare registered scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack against the START reference sequence after each clk_en tick. Explicitly check the contrasting side of REQ-0097's observation: without reset, sda_oen follows ordinary command behavior and is driven low during START instead of being forced high by reset.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then deassert nReset and provide at least two rising edges of clk with ena=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: after reset initialization, cscl and csda are both 1, representing the idle-high synchronized SCL and SDA bus state; reset also leaves the module ready to resume sampling.
elements.check_method: At reset assertion and after reset release, sample the cscl and csda probes after each rising edge and compare against the reset/reference model, requiring both values to initialize high.

elements.stimulus: Complete the nReset reset sequence with ena=1, then drive scl_i and sda_i through stable post-reset changes, for example from 1/1 to 0/1 and later to 0/0, holding each combination for enough clk cycles for the two-stage synchronizers to update.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: cscl and csda must not remain fixed at their reset-high values; after the expected synchronization latency, cscl reflects scl_i and csda reflects sda_i for each stable input combination, continuously sampling the external bus after reset.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate two-stage synchronizer reference model. Compare cscl and csda on every rising edge after the modeled latency, including both transitions and stable intervals, and require no missed or permanently stuck sample.

elements.stimulus: After reset deassertion, drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=1, hold both values stable through a rising edge of clk, then drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 and hold those values stable through the next rising edge. Continue clocking without changing the inputs.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: on each rising edge, the raw scl_i and sda_i values present at that edge are captured into the two-stage cSCL and cSDA path. The synchronized cscl/csda probes show the sampled values with the expected two-stage pipeline latency, and the second pattern replaces the first only after the corresponding capture delay.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, sample scl_i, sda_i, cscl, and csda after nonblocking assignments settle. Compare cscl/csda against a two-stage reference model whose first stage receives the raw inputs on that edge and whose second stage receives the prior first-stage values; require exact cycle-by-cycle agreement.

elements.stimulus: Hold scl_i=0 and sda_i=1 through a rising edge of clk. Change scl_i to 1 and sda_i to 0 only immediately after that edge, keep the new values stable through the remainder of the cycle, and then clock through subsequent rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of shows: the post-edge input changes are not captured on the preceding rising edge, so cscl/csda do not reflect the new values as if they had been sampled at that edge. The new values enter the two-stage capture path only on the next rising edge and appear at the synchronized probes after the normal two-stage latency.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model driven only by the values of scl_i and sda_i sampled at each posedge clk. Assert that cscl/csda remain consistent with the prior sampled values immediately after the change and then match the delayed model when the next edge samples the new values.

elements.stimulus: After reset has initialized the capture state high, drive scl_i and sda_i to low and hold them stable across successive posedges of clk; then drive both inputs high and hold them stable across at least three more posedges.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement's observation: cscl and csda change from their initialized or prior values only through the two-stage synchronous capture, with the new stable scl_i and sda_i values observable at the synchronized capture output after the expected two capture clock stages, and thereafter remain equal to the held inputs. They must not respond combinationally between clock edges.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, sample cscl and csda after nonblocking assignments settle and compare against a cycle-accurate two-stage reference model in which stage 1 captures scl_i/sda_i and stage 2 captures stage 1. Assert no changes between posedges and assert the expected delayed values for both signals.

elements.stimulus: With the capture state initialized high, drive scl_i and sda_i low for only one clock interval, returning both inputs high immediately after the next posedge, and repeat with the transition occurring at varying offsets around a posedge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting, non-holding side of the observation: cscl and csda must not mirror the raw one-interval excursion immediately or asynchronously. Any observed low value must occur only at the synchronized two-stage capture latency and only as predicted by the sampled first-stage value; after the excursion has propagated, both outputs return high through the same staged latency. No cscl/csda change is permitted between clock edges.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed cscl/csda traces with a two-stage sampled reference model for each transition offset. Flag any first-stage/direct-path response at the input transition, any asynchronous output change, or any output sequence that differs from the model's delayed propagation and return behavior.

elements.stimulus: After reset is released, drive scl_i and sda_i to stable high levels, then to stable low levels, holding each level long enough for the two-stage capture registers cscl/csda to acquire it and for multiple filter sampling intervals to expire. Repeat with stable high levels.
elements.expected_response: The captured values cscl and csda follow the synchronized scl_i and sda_i inputs. After sufficient filter samples, the majority-filtered outputs sscl and ssda follow the corresponding captured levels: high for stable high input and low for stable low input, demonstrating that captured bus values are passed through the digital input filtering stage.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after synchronizer and filter updates settle, compare cscl/csda and sscl/ssda against a reference model of the two-stage capture, filter sampling interval, three-sample histories, and majority function. Require the filtered outputs to converge to each stable captured input without using raw-input timing.

elements.stimulus: Establish stable high scl_i and sda_i so cscl/csda and sscl/ssda are high. Apply a short low pulse to scl_i and independently to sda_i, timed so the low level is captured in cscl or csda for no more than one filter sample before returning high; then continue stable high long enough for subsequent filter samples.
elements.expected_response: The captured value for the pulsed signal may change low, but the filtered output for that signal does not change to low when the three-sample majority remains high; it stays high or returns high according to the filter history. The unaffected signal's cs* and ss* remain high. This is the contrasting case showing that the filtering stage does not pass an insufficient captured transition directly to sscl/ssda.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for capture, filter sampling, history shifting, and majority evaluation. Check that the relevant cscl/csda transition is observable while sscl/ssda suppresses the one-sample disturbance, and check that no filtered transition is reported for the suppressed pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, drive stable raw scl_i and sda_i values, and run posedge clk cycles long enough for the two-stage synchronizers and the filter counter to reach an expiration. Change the synchronized input values before a subsequent filter expiration and continue running.
elements.expected_response: Requirement-holds side of the sampling behavior: when filter_cnt expires, fscl and fsda each shift in the current synchronized SCL and SDA samples, respectively. The histories retain their prior values between expirations.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage synchronizers and sampling interval clk_cnt >> 2. At every filter_cnt expiration compare the observed fscl and fsda history shifts against the model, and verify that the new samples correspond to the synchronized inputs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, drive stable scl_i and sda_i values, and observe several enabled clocks for which the reference-model filter counter is nonzero and has not expired. Repeat after changing the synchronized input values but before the next expiration.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding side of the sampling behavior: while the derived filter interval has not expired, fscl and fsda do not shift and remain equal to their previous history values, even if synchronized input samples are available.
elements.check_method: Use the reference counter model to identify enabled cycles with filter_cnt nonzero and no expiration. Assert that fscl and fsda are unchanged on those cycles; separately confirm that the next expiration produces the expected shift.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive clk_cnt=0, then run consecutive posedge clk cycles while driving changing stable scl_i and sda_i patterns long enough for synchronization. Repeat with clk_cnt=1.
elements.expected_response: Boundary interval case: because floor(clk_cnt >> 2) is zero for clk_cnt=0 and 1, the filter sampling interval is treated as the minimum enabled interval; fscl and fsda shift synchronized SCL and SDA samples on every enabled filter-sampling opportunity rather than becoming stuck waiting for a nonzero counter.
elements.check_method: Compare fscl and fsda on every enabled clock with a reference model implementing clk_cnt >> 2 and the specified zero-interval handling. Check that histories advance at the minimum interval and that no filter counter deadlock occurs.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset and rst inactive, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4 so the filter sampling interval is enabled. After synchronization settling, drive sampled SCL values [1,1,0] and sampled SDA values [0,0,1] on three successive filter_cnt expiries, holding each raw input long enough for the two-stage synchronizers to capture it.
elements.expected_response: On each filter_cnt expiry, new synchronized values are shifted into the respective three-sample histories. For the final histories, the majority-filtered outputs are sscl=1 for SCL history [1,1,0] and ssda=0 for SDA history [0,0,1]; this is the majority-true and majority-false outcome respectively.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the synchronizers, filter sampling interval, history shifting, and three-input majority function. At every filter_cnt expiry compare the observed fscl/fsda history updates and sscl/ssda outputs with the model, allowing for registered probe update timing.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset and rst inactive, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, and allow synchronization to settle. Drive sampled SCL values [0,0,1] and sampled SDA values [1,1,0] on three successive filter_cnt expiries, holding each raw input long enough for the two-stage synchronizers to capture it.
elements.expected_response: On each filter_cnt expiry, synchronized samples are shifted into the histories. For the final histories, the majority-filtered outputs are sscl=0 for SCL history [0,0,1] and ssda=1 for SDA history [1,1,0], demonstrating the contrasting majority result for both signals.
elements.check_method: Compute expected three-sample histories and their majority values with a cycle-accurate reference model, then compare sscl and ssda immediately after each registered filter update; specifically require the final outputs sscl=0 and ssda=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4. Drive scl_i and sda_i high long enough for synchronization and three filter samples, then drive each line to a stable low level and hold it long enough for three corresponding synchronized samples. Account for synchronizer and filter latency when applying and observing the samples.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observation: sscl and ssda equal the three-sample majority value for their respective synchronized sample histories. After the histories become predominantly high, the filtered signals are high; after they become predominantly low, the filtered signals are low and remain stable while the raw inputs remain stable. The filtered signals therefore represent the stable internal SCL and SDA lines rather than an unsynchronized instantaneous sample.
elements.check_method: At each filter sampling event, calculate the expected majority of the corresponding three synchronized SCL and SDA samples in a reference model and compare it with the sscl and ssda probes after registered updates. Check that each filtered output changes only to the modeled majority value and remains unchanged during stable input intervals.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=4, and both filtered outputs established high, inject a single filter-sampling interval of scl_i=0 and sda_i=0, then restore both raw lines high. The disturbance must be shorter than required to make two of the three synchronized history samples low; afterward hold both raw lines high for additional filter samples.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting/non-holding side of the observation: sscl and ssda remain high throughout the short raw-line disturbance because the three-sample majority remains high; no filtered low level is produced from the isolated glitch. Once stable high samples continue, sscl and ssda remain high, demonstrating that the internal signals used as stable SCL and SDA versions reject a disturbance that does not change the majority-filtered histories.
elements.check_method: Use the synchronizer/filter reference model to predict each three-sample majority during and after the injected pulse, then compare sscl and ssda cycle-by-cycle. Assert that neither probe falls for the isolated disturbance and that both match the modeled majority after subsequent samples.

elements.stimulus: Release both bus lines, apply asynchronous reset, then operate with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. After the initialized filtered signals are high, drive scl_i low and sda_i low and hold both values long enough for synchronization and the three-sample majority filter to produce filtered SCL and SDA falling transitions.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after each filtered transition, dscl and dsda contain the preceding filtered sscl and ssda values, and on the following registered update become the newly filtered values. The delayed signals therefore reproduce the filtered SCL and SDA histories with the specified register delay.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after settled nonblocking updates, compare dscl[n] with the prior sampled sscl[n-1] and dsda[n] with prior sampled ssda[n-1] using a cycle-accurate reference model of synchronization, filtering, and delayed-register updates. Check both falling transitions.

elements.stimulus: Continue operating with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 after TP-0000, holding scl_i and sda_i steadily low for multiple enabled clocks, then hold them steadily high for multiple enabled clocks so the filtered signals settle high again without introducing additional transitions.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-transition case: while sscl and ssda remain unchanged, dscl and dsda remain equal to those unchanged filtered values on every clock; no independent or spurious delayed transition occurs. When the stable high transition eventually occurs, each delayed signal changes only on the corresponding delayed update.
elements.check_method: Use assertions that dscl and dsda remain stable whenever sscl and ssda respectively remain stable, and compare each subsequent delayed value against the prior-cycle filtered value. Confirm the stable-low and stable-high intervals and the delayed rising transitions with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1, establish a stable filtered bus with scl_i high and sda_i high, then drive sda_i low and hold both lines stable for enough enabled clocks to populate the synchronizer and three-sample filter histories.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered SDA changes from high to low while filtered SCL is high, the current filtered SDA differs from delayed filtered SDA, a filtered START event is detected, and busy rises. This is the event-detected side of the busy behavior specified by REQ-0106.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for two-stage synchronization, filter sampling, majority filtering, and delayed-value update. At the cycle where ssda=0, dsda=1, and sscl=1, compare the observed busy transition against busy rising on the following registered update; also check sta_condition if available.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and filtered SCL held high, first establish filtered SDA low and busy asserted, then drive sda_i high and hold it stable for enough enabled clocks to pass synchronization and majority filtering.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered SDA changes from low to high while filtered SCL is high, the current filtered SDA differs from delayed filtered SDA, a filtered STOP event is detected, and busy falls. This is the event-detected side of the busy behavior specified by REQ-0106.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the cycle where ssda=1, dsda=0, and sscl=1, then compare busy against a fall on the following registered update; also check sto_condition if available.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, hold filtered SCL low while toggling sda_i, and separately hold filtered SCL high while keeping sda_i unchanged; apply each input long enough for synchronization and filtering to complete.
elements.expected_response: When current filtered SDA equals delayed filtered SDA, or when filtered SDA changes while filtered SCL is low, no START or STOP bus event is detected and busy remains unchanged. This is the no-event side of the busy behavior specified by REQ-0106.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to verify either ssda equals dsda or sscl=0 at every filtered update, then assert that busy has no transition and sta_condition and sto_condition remain deasserted.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0, then release nReset and keep rst=0 and ena=1. Set clk_cnt=0. With scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, run enough posedges for the synchronizer, filter histories, and delayed filtered SDA to settle high. Then keep scl_i=1 and drive sda_i=0 for enough enabled clocks to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered transition occurs with filtered SCL high, sta_condition asserts, representing detection of an I2C START condition. It is not asserted before the filtered SDA falling transition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the two-stage synchronization, three-sample filtering, and delayed filtered SDA. Compare the predicted filtered transition condition against the sta_condition probe and require sta_condition=1 on the modeled qualifying cycle.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0, then release nReset and keep rst=0 and ena=1. Set clk_cnt=0. With scl_i=0 and sda_i=1, run enough posedges for the filtered signals to settle. While filtered SCL remains low, drive sda_i=0 long enough to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition, then keep both inputs stable.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is low does not satisfy the START condition; sta_condition remains 0 for the transition and subsequent stable interval. This is the non-qualifying side of the requirement's condition.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate synchronization and filter reference model to identify the filtered SDA falling edge and verify modeled filtered SCL=0 on that edge. Assert that sta_condition is never high for this stimulus.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000. Hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 for enough enabled rising edges to establish filtered sSCL=1 and sSDA=0. Then drive sda_i=1 while keeping scl_i=1 for enough enabled rising edges to propagate through synchronization and the three-sample majority filter, producing a filtered SDA low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered transition occurs with filtered SCL high, the controller detects the STOP condition and asserts sto_condition for the corresponding detection interval. This is the holding case of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, majority histories, delayed filtered SDA, and sto_condition expression. Compare the predicted sto_condition assertion cycle-by-cycle with the DUT probe after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000. Hold scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 for enough enabled rising edges to establish filtered sSCL=0 and filtered sSDA=0. Then drive sda_i=1 while keeping scl_i=0 for enough enabled rising edges to produce a filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL remains low.
elements.expected_response: The controller does not detect a STOP condition and sto_condition remains deasserted for the entire transition. This is the non-holding case of the requirement: an SDA rise without filtered SCL high must not assert sto_condition.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate synchronization, filtering, delayed-value, and STOP-detection reference model, and compare sto_condition at every posedge. Confirm that no assertion occurs during or after the filtered SDA transition while filtered SCL is low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i high and sda_i high to establish an idle bus. With ena high, drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i high for sufficient synchronizer and filter sampling time for a filtered SDA high-to-low transition; do not issue a STOP transition.
elements.expected_response: When sta_condition is asserted for the filtered START, busy updates high on the corresponding registered status update and remains high while no filtered STOP is detected. This exercises the 'busy is high after START detection' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SDA falling transition while filtered SCL is high and compare busy after the associated posedge update; assert busy is 1 from that update until a separately detected STOP.

elements.stimulus: First establish busy high using a filtered START as in TP-0000. While scl_i remains high and the filtered SDA is low, drive sda_i high for sufficient synchronizer and filter sampling time for a filtered SDA low-to-high transition, creating a filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: When sto_condition is asserted for the filtered STOP, busy updates low on the corresponding registered status update and remains low afterward in the absence of another filtered START. This exercises the 'busy is low after STOP detection' side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SDA rising transition while filtered SCL is high and compare busy after the associated posedge update; assert busy is 0 from that update onward unless a new filtered START is detected.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a supported READ command (cmd=1000) on a rising edge, and model the bus released high initially. When the READ sequence reaches its released-SCL read window, hold scl_i low externally while the DUT has scl_oen=1; keep sda_i stable, then release scl_i high and allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observed behavior: scl_oen remains 1 while filtered SCL is low, the READ phase and timing do not advance to the next low phase, and the subsequent scl_oen transition to 0 is postponed until filtered SCL becomes high and synchronized low-period timing completes. Bus-status filtering continues during the wait.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of synchronization, filtering, slave-wait, and clk_en. At every settled posedge, compare scl_oen and command completion timing; assert that no scl_oen=0 transition occurs while the filtered SCL is low and that the transition occurs after release and the required enabled timing boundary.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a supported WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1, and provide a released-high bus. During the WRITE released-SCL high phase, externally force scl_i low to emulate another master, hold it low long enough to pass the input filter, then release it high and keep SDA high so arbitration is not lost.
elements.expected_response: This is the multi-master synchronization side of the observed behavior: the externally forced filtered SCL falling edge causes the controller to postpone its normal scl_oen transition to 0, reload and resynchronize its low-period timing, and only transition scl_oen to 0 after filtered SCL is high and the synchronized timing completes. The command continues without arbitration loss or spurious acknowledgement.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen together with filtered SCL, the scl_sync probe, clk_en, and cmd_ack. Compare against a reference model requiring scl_sync and counter reload on the released-high SCL falling edge, no premature scl_oen=0 transition, and normal completion after resynchronization.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue a supported READ command (cmd=1000) on a rising edge, and keep scl_i and sda_i high throughout the released-SCL read window with no external SCL falling edge or clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: This is the ordinary, non-holding side of the observed behavior: scl_oen does not remain postponed by an external condition and transitions to 0 at the normal next enabled phase boundary after the released-high phase and required timing complete; the command then proceeds to its normal completion.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for clk_en, filtering, and READ phase timing. Compare the observed scl_oen waveform and cmd_ack against the no-stretch/no-synchronization prediction, and assert that the low-phase transition occurs at the first permitted enabled boundary rather than a later postponed boundary.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, and issue a supported WRITE command while allowing the command sequence to reach a phase where scl_oen becomes 1. At that point, externally hold scl_i low long enough for the synchronizer and filter to make sscl=0, while keeping ena=1.
elements.expected_response: When scl_oen=1 and the filtered SCL sscl remains 0 during the active command, slave_wait asserts. The timing counter and command FSM remain paused and do not advance to the next timing phase while the filtered SCL is low. This is the holding side of the observed scl_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge clk, compare scl_oen, sscl, slave_wait, clk_en, and the command-phase probe against a reference model including synchronization, filtering, and clock-stretch pause behavior. Require slave_wait=1 throughout the released-SCL/filtered-low interval and require no FSM progress or clk_en tick caused by elapsed command timing during that interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, and issue the same supported WRITE command while allowing the command sequence to reach a phase where scl_oen becomes 1. Release the external SCL line so scl_i remains high long enough for the synchronizer and filter to make sscl=1.
elements.expected_response: When scl_oen=1 and the filtered SCL sscl is high, slave_wait remains deasserted, and the command timing is allowed to progress on clk_en ticks. This is the contrasting non-holding side of the observed scl_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge clk, compare scl_oen, sscl, slave_wait, clk_en, and the command-phase probe against the reference model. Require slave_wait=0 for the released-SCL/filtered-high interval and require subsequent command-phase progress, distinguishing this result from the filtered-low case.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, and a valid clk_cnt, issue a supported command such as READ. Model the external bus as holding SCL low (scl_i=0) while allowing the controller to release SCL (observe scl_oen=1); continue clocks until the synchronized and filtered SCL value is low (sscl=0).
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: slave_wait asserts while scl_oen=1 and sscl=0, indicating that an external slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low. The command timing phase does not advance while the condition persists.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the slave_wait probe against the reference model condition scl_oen && !sscl. Verify that slave_wait becomes 1 after the filtered-low condition is established and remains 1 while the external hold persists; also verify no command-phase progress occurs during the wait.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted and ena high, issue the same supported command and allow the external bus to release SCL high (scl_i=1) when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1). Continue clocks until synchronization and filtering establish sscl=1.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding contrast of the requirement: slave_wait remains 0 when SCL is released and the filtered SCL is high, because no external participant is holding SCL low. The command may proceed to its next timing phase on the applicable clk_en tick.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the slave_wait probe against the reference model condition scl_oen && !sscl. Confirm slave_wait is not asserted throughout the released-high, filtered-high interval and that normal FSM progression resumes on clk_en.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a supported READ command on an enabled clock and wait until the READ sample window is reached and scl_oen=1. Then externally drive scl_i low and hold the bus low long enough for synchronization and filtering to make sscl=0 and slave_wait=1, while keeping ena=1 and the command inputs stable. Hold the low SCL for at least four enabled-clock opportunities.
elements.expected_response: While slave_wait=1, scl_oen remains 1 and sda_oen remains at the values from the current command phase; neither output enable changes to the next bit-timing phase despite enabled-clock opportunities. The timing counter remains paused and the bit-level FSM does not advance. This is the holding-side behavior of the requirement's port difference.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, record scl_oen, sda_oen, clk_en, slave_wait, and the active command phase. Assert that for every sampled cycle with slave_wait=1, both output enables equal their values at slave_wait entry and the reference-model phase and counter are unchanged. Confirm the external bus model keeps filtered SCL low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue the same supported READ command on an enabled clock and wait until the READ sample window is reached and scl_oen=1. Keep the external SCL line released high by driving scl_i=1, with no clock stretching, for multiple enabled-clock opportunities; then continue until the READ phase completes or the next SCL-low phase is entered.
elements.expected_response: With slave_wait inactive, the active command sequence advances on clk_en and scl_oen eventually changes from its released-high value to the next command-phase value; sda_oen also changes whenever required by the next phase. This is the contrasting otherwise-side behavior of the requirement's port difference.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge clk, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against a reference FSM driven by clk_en. Assert slave_wait remains 0 while filtered SCL is high, and assert that the command phase and at least scl_oen transition after an enabled-clock opportunity, unlike the held-low case.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and a valid clk_cnt, issue a command that reaches a phase where scl_oen=1 and SCL is released high. Hold scl_i high until the released-high phase is established, then drive scl_i low long enough for the two-stage synchronizer and majority filter to make sscl fall. Continue clocking with ena high.
elements.expected_response: The holding side of the requirement applies: when the filtered SCL falls while scl_oen=1, scl_sync asserts. The timing counter reloads and local low-period timing restarts in synchronization with the externally forced SCL low; the FSM does not proceed using the pre-fall timing schedule.
elements.check_method: At each posedge, compare scl_sync, clk_en/cnt_zero, and subsequent phase timing against a reference model containing the synchronizer, filter, edge detector, counter reload, and low-period restart. Confirm scl_sync is asserted for the modeled synchronization event and that the next timing interval begins from the reload value rather than the prior counter value.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and the same valid clk_cnt, issue a command that reaches a phase where scl_oen=1 and SCL is released high. Keep scl_i high continuously for multiple divider and filter intervals, with no external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: The non-holding side of the requirement applies: scl_sync remains deasserted, no external-fall counter reload occurs, and local low-period timing follows the ordinary divider schedule without synchronization to an external SCL-low interval.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to predict filtered SCL, scl_sync, counter expiration, clk_en ticks, and phase progression. Assert that no filtered SCL falling edge is detected, scl_sync never pulses, and counter reloads occur only at ordinary divider events.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the released-high bus idle. Issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0 twice, first with clk_cnt=1 and then with clk_cnt=8, waiting for cmd_ack and returning to idle between trials. Record the acceptance cycle and the single-cycle cmd_ack cycle for each trial; exclude arbitration loss, clock stretching, and multi-master SCL synchronization.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the requirement: cmd_ack occurs only after the WRITE bit-timing phases have advanced on cnt-generated clk_en ticks, and the measured command-completion latency for clk_cnt=8 is greater than the latency for clk_cnt=1 by the expected counter-paced amount.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for cnt reload, decrement, expiration, clk_en generation, and WRITE phase advancement. Compare observed cmd_ack latency from command acceptance against the model for both clk_cnt values and assert that the larger reload value produces the correspondingly longer latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and the released-high bus idle. Issue identical supported START commands in separate trials using clk_cnt=1 and clk_cnt=8, and observe cmd_ack from command acceptance through completion. Do not apply clock stretching, arbitration loss, or multi-master synchronization.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise/non-holding side of the requirement and must be rejected: cmd_ack must not occur with the same timing for both clk_cnt values, and it must not complete without the counter-paced bit-timing delay. The observed latency must vary with clk_cnt and match the cnt-paced timing model.
elements.check_method: Measure the number of posedges between command acceptance and the registered cmd_ack pulse for both trials. Fail if the latencies are equal when the reference model predicts a difference, or if cmd_ack occurs before the required cnt-generated timing ticks and START phases.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset inactive, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, keep the bus released-high, issue a supported START command while idle, and hold clk_cnt and ena constant until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: cmd_ack is a single-clock pulse only after the START timing phases have advanced at the cadence established by cnt loading from clk_cnt=3 and decrementing once per enabled clock; the measured intervals between timing-enable-driven phase advances and the terminal acknowledgement match the reference model.
elements.check_method: At each posedge sample cmd_ack after registered updates settle. Compare the acknowledgement cycle and all observable phase-duration intervals against a cycle-accurate reference model whose counter reloads from 3 and decrements on each enabled clock; require exactly one cmd_ack pulse and no early or late pulse.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset inactive, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, issue a supported START command, then deassert ena for several clocks during the active command and reassert ena=1 while holding clk_cnt constant; wait for completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: while ena=0, cmd_ack does not arrive at the prescaled cadence because timing progression is disabled; after ena returns high, the command resumes and cmd_ack occurs at the remaining cadence predicted by the counter reference model, rather than at a time corresponding to decrementing during the disabled interval.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack cycle-by-cycle and compare against a reference model that suppresses counter decrement and timing-enable events while ena=0, reloads or pauses as specified for the disabled interval, and resumes when ena=1. Require no acknowledgement during the pause and exactly one correctly timed acknowledgement after re-enabling.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3. Allow the internal counter to reload, then provide enabled rising-edge clock cycles until the counter reaches zero, keeping nReset=1 and rst=0.
elements.expected_response: When the counter expires, the module asserts clk_en for the timing-enable event used by the command FSM. This is the holding side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, compare the observed clk_en pulse with a reference divider model loaded from clk_cnt=3 and decremented only while ena is high; require clk_en=1 on the modeled expiration event.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3. Start a counter interval and sample clk_en on the first enabled clock cycles before the modeled counter expiration, without asserting either reset.
elements.expected_response: While the counter has not expired, the module does not assert clk_en; it remains low. This is the contrasting non-holding side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference divider model to identify enabled cycles preceding cnt_zero and compare the registered clk_en observation on each such cycle; require clk_en=0 before the expiration event.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, and a released-high bus. Issue a supported START command and keep the command active. Record clk_en, scl_oen, and sda_oen on every posedge through completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: between successive clk_en assertions, scl_oen and sda_oen remain at the current START bit-timing phase values. Each transition to the next START phase occurs only on a posedge where clk_en is asserted, and the command eventually reaches its normal completion sequence.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the prescaler and START phase sequence. At every posedge, assert that any change in scl_oen or sda_oen is accompanied by clk_en=1; compare the observed phase sequence and cmd_ack against the model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8. Issue a supported WRITE command with din=1 on a released-high bus. During each active WRITE phase, sample scl_oen and sda_oen on every posedge, including all cycles after a phase begins and before the next predicted clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise side of shows: a nonconforming DUT would change scl_oen or sda_oen to the next phase, or reach the completion output sequence, during a cycle with clk_en=0 and before the preceding timed interval expires. Such an early transition must not occur; any detected output change with clk_en=0 is a failure, while the compliant response is to hold the current phase until clk_en=1.
elements.check_method: Inject an assertion that scl_oen and sda_oen are stable across every posedge-to-posedge interval whose ending sample has clk_en=0, unless reset or arbitration loss applies. Correlate any transition with the reference divider and report a failure for a phase transition or completion occurring before the next clk_en assertion.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset=0 and release it, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=1, and provide a released-high bus. Accept a START command on an enabled timing tick, then drive ena=0 before the command reaches its terminal completion phase and hold ena=0 for at least the remaining command duration predicted by the reference model.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the requirement: cmd_ack remains low throughout the ena-low interval and no command-completion pulse occurs; normal bit-level FSM timing is paused while disabled and the command cannot complete during that interval.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after ena falls, compare cmd_ack against a reference model with the timing counter reloaded and FSM advancement disabled; assert that cmd_ack is 0 for the entire disabled interval and that no completion pulse occurs at the originally expected enabled completion cycle.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, clk_cnt=1, released-high bus, and accepted START command, but keep ena=1 continuously until the command reaches its terminal completion phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: with ena high, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock when the START command completes.
elements.check_method: Use the enabled reference timing model to predict the terminal phase and compare sampled cmd_ack after each posedge; require one and only one high cycle at completion, with cmd_ack low before and after that pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 1, hold the bus released and SCL/SDA high, drive din=1, and apply cmd=0100 (WRITE) while idle; continue clocking until the WRITE sequence reaches its stable SCL-high phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: after WRITE acceptance, sda_chk is asserted during the stable high phase of the WRITE bit, enabling arbitration checking; it is deasserted outside that phase and the WRITE eventually completes with a one-clock cmd_ack if no arbitration loss occurs.
