elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase probes to identify the active WRITE phase, then compare sda_chk against the reference FSM expectation on every posedge: sda_chk must be 1 in the stable high phase and 0 in other phases; also verify no unexpected al and the single cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt to 1, hold the bus released and SCL/SDA high, and apply cmd=1000 (READ) while idle; allow the complete READ sequence to execute, including the read sample window and command completion.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the requirement: because the active operation is READ rather than WRITE, sda_chk remains deasserted throughout the READ sequence, including its SCL-high sampling window; no arbitration-check enable is generated.
elements.check_method: Use the read_sequence and read_sample_window probes to delimit the READ operation and sample sda_chk after each posedge; assert that sda_chk is 0 for the entire interval from READ acceptance through cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a valid released-high I2C bus, set din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE=4 on an enabled clk_en tick. Follow the WRITE data-setup phase through the next enabled tick into the stable high phase, keeping the external SDA and SCL lines high.
elements.expected_response: While write_stable_high_phase is asserted, sda_chk is 1. This is the holding side of the observed behavior: scl_oen is 1 and remains released high, while sda_oen retains the value selected by din (sda_oen=1 for din=1).
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered updates settle, compare sda_chk, write_stable_high_phase, scl_oen, and sda_oen against a WRITE phase reference model; require sda_chk=1 throughout the stable high phase and require the released-SCL and din-selected-SDA output-enable values.

elements.stimulus: Using the same reset, ena=1, din=1, released-high bus, and accepted cmd=WRITE=4 sequence, sample the WRITE data-setup phase before the enabled clk_en tick that enters the stable high phase, and then sample the subsequent SCL-low phase after the stable high phase ends.
elements.expected_response: When write_stable_high_phase is 0, sda_chk is 0; the stable-high assertion is absent. In the preceding data-setup phase, scl_oen remains asserted low rather than released high, and after the phase ends the controller returns SCL low, demonstrating the contrasting non-holding behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the phase reference model and cycle-by-cycle waveform comparison at settled posedge samples; require sda_chk=0 for both non-stable intervals and verify scl_oen is not the stable-high released value during the setup/low phases.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1 while the bus is initially high. After the WRITE command reaches its stable high phase with sda_oen=1 and sda_chk=1, externally hold SDA low by driving sda_i=0 long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to produce ssda=0.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in observed_via.shows: while the controller expects SDA released high, sda_oen remains 1, and filtered SDA is low, the arbitration-lost output al asserts on the next registered update and remains asserted until reset.
elements.check_method: Use the write_stable_high_phase, sda_chk, sda_oen, and ssda probes to qualify the condition; compare the sampled al output against a reference model on each posedge clk and verify al becomes 1 after the filtered-low condition.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, deassert it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=1 while the bus remains high. When the WRITE command reaches its stable high phase with sda_oen=1 and sda_chk=1, keep the external SDA line released high so synchronized and filtered SDA remain high (ssda=1).
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise case in observed_via.shows: because filtered SDA is not low during the stable-high WRITE phase, al does not assert for this phase.
elements.check_method: Use the write_stable_high_phase, sda_chk, sda_oen, and ssda probes to qualify the non-loss condition; sample al after every posedge clk through completion and compare against a reference model requiring al=0 throughout, absent any other arbitration-loss stimulus.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and a released-high bus, issue a supported non-STOP command such as START on an enabled timing tick. After active_command is asserted and before the command completes, drive SDA from filtered high to filtered low and back to high while filtered SCL remains high, with the transition stable long enough to produce sto_condition.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP-detection event while the non-STOP command is active, al asserts and remains asserted; the active command aborts, both scl_oen and sda_oen release, and cmd_ack is not generated for the aborted command. This is the al-asserts side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-line and FSM reference model to identify sto_condition while active_command is asserted with cmd equal to START, WRITE, or READ. Compare sampled al, output enables, and cmd_ack after the registered update; require al to transition low-to-high at that event and remain high until reset, with no completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and a released-high bus, issue the STOP command on an enabled timing tick and allow its normal sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, and release SDA while filtered SCL is high, producing the command's intentional filtered STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: The intentional STOP condition for the active STOP command does not newly assert al; the STOP sequence completes with a one-clock cmd_ack and returns the FSM to idle. This is the no-al-exception side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Decode the accepted command as STOP and correlate the intentional sto_condition with stop_sequence. Sample al and cmd_ack after each posedge; require al to remain low throughout and require exactly one completion pulse at the end of the STOP sequence.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue an enabled WRITE command with din=1. During the WRITE stable-high phase, externally hold SDA low while the DUT has released SDA high; keep SCL available high so arbitration checking occurs and do not assert either reset.
elements.expected_response: When al rises, the arbitration-loss response must return the bit-level FSM to idle and, on the registered output update immediately following the indication, set scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1. This is the holding side of the observed_via behavior: both lines are released rather than retaining the active command phase.
elements.check_method: Use a scoreboard synchronized to posedge clk. Detect the rising edge of al, then on the next settled registered-output sample assert idle=1, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1; also verify no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted command. Record bins for arbitration-loss detection and both output enables released.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue an enabled WRITE command with din=0 and provide normal bus conditions. Observe the active WRITE data-drive phase before command completion, with no external arbitration loss or unexpected STOP.
elements.expected_response: The ordinary active-command behavior must be retained: al does not rise, the FSM does not enter the arbitration-loss idle response, and sda_oen remains 0 while the WRITE bit drives SDA low (with scl_oen reflecting the current WRITE timing phase). This is the contrasting otherwise side of the observed_via behavior: the enables reflect the active command phase and are not forced to both 1 by arbitration-loss handling.
elements.check_method: At the registered output samples identified as the WRITE data-drive phase, assert al=0 and sda_oen=0; compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the normal WRITE phase reference model and ensure they are not both forced to 1 before normal completion. Record bins for ordinary active WRITE output control and absence of arbitration loss.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) with ena=1. During read_sample_window, arrange for filtered SCL (sscl) to rise while filtered SDA (ssda) is stable at 1, while driving sda_i so that the synchronized and filtered value at the sampling edge is distinguishable from the raw input value.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge within the READ sample window, dout captures ssda=1, regardless of the instantaneous raw sda_i value. This is the holding case of observed_via.shows: dout captures the value of the filtered SDA signal ssda.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to predict ssda and the filtered SCL rising edge; sample dout after the corresponding posedge and compare it exactly with predicted ssda. Also confirm that the comparison is against filtered ssda, not raw sda_i.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ and complete one filtered SCL rising-edge sample. Then, while no filtered SCL rising edge is occurring in the READ sample window, change the bus input and allow the filter to change ssda from its previously sampled value to the opposite value.
elements.expected_response: dout retains its previously sampled value and does not update merely because ssda changed outside a filtered SCL rising edge within the READ sample window. This is the non-holding case of observed_via.shows: dout does not capture the filtered SDA value when the sampling condition is absent.
elements.check_method: Track filtered ssda and filtered SCL edges with the reference model; assert that dout changes only on the qualifying filtered SCL rising edge and remains unchanged on cycles where ssda changes without that sampling event.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so dout is 0. With ena=1, issue a READ command and provide a released-high SCL bus with external SDA held high long enough for synchronization and filtering. Allow the READ sequence to release SCL and produce a filtered SCL rising edge while the filtered SDA value is 1.
elements.expected_response: For the filtered-SCL rising-edge capture event, dout updates from 0 to the current filtered SDA value 1. This is the required `shows` behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge and compare dout in that cycle against the modeled filtered SDA value; require dout=1 and a one-cycle registered update at the event.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so dout is 0. With ena=1, issue a READ command and hold the externally released SCL low so the filtered SCL remains low. Change external SDA from low to high and hold it long enough for the filtered SDA to become 1, but do not allow a filtered SCL rising edge during the observation interval.
elements.expected_response: Because no filtered-SCL rising-edge capture event occurs, dout does not update to the current filtered SDA value; it remains 0. This is the contrasting `otherwise` behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to confirm filtered SDA changes to 1 while filtered SCL has no rising edge, then compare dout on every settled posedge clk and require it to remain at its pre-event value 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ (1000) while idle, and provide a released-high SCL bus. Drive filtered SDA to 0, allow the READ sample window to assert, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge. Repeat the sample event with filtered SDA driven to 1 and produce another filtered SCL rising edge before command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on each filtered SCL rising edge while read_sample_window is asserted, dout updates on the corresponding registered clock update to the current filtered SDA value: first 0, then 1. These values are available as the received data bits for the READ operation.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter histories, majority-filtered SDA/SCL, and filtered SCL edge detection. At each modeled filtered SCL rising edge in the READ sample window, compare dout after the posedge and NBA settling to the modeled filtered SDA value; verify both 0 and 1 samples.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ (1000) while idle, and reach the READ sample window with filtered SCL high. Establish dout=0 from an earlier valid sample, then change the external SDA input so that filtered SDA becomes 1 while keeping filtered SCL high and preventing any filtered SCL rising edge. Hold this condition for multiple enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs during the READ sampling event, dout does not update to the new filtered SDA value and remains 0 throughout the interval.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to confirm that filtered SDA changes while filtered SCL has no rising transition. Sample dout after each posedge and NBA settling, and assert that it retains its previous value rather than matching the changed filtered SDA.

elements.stimulus: After reset has completed and idle is asserted, set ena=1, drive cmd=START (4'b0001), and choose clk_cnt=16'd4. Hold cmd and ena stable while observing cycles in which clk_en=0 before the next timing-enable tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observation: while a valid START command is pending and clk_en=0, the command FSM remains idle; idle stays asserted and no command execution phase begins.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after registered updates settle, compare the idle probe against a reference divider/FSM model and assert idle==1 on all sampled cycles where ena==1, cmd==START, and clk_en==0 before the first permitted advancement.

elements.stimulus: After reset has completed and idle is asserted, set ena=1, drive cmd=START (4'b0001), and hold it through the first cycle where clk_en becomes 1, with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 so the START sequence can proceed normally.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of the observation: when the valid START command is pending and clk_en=1, the FSM advances from idle into the START command sequence; idle deasserts after the corresponding registered state update.
elements.check_method: Detect the first enabled tick with cmd=START and verify in the post-posedge waveform that idle transitions from 1 to 0 and start_sequence or another active-command indication becomes asserted, matching the reference FSM model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the bus released high, wait until idle=1, present cmd=START (0001), and hold it through a clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: The START command is decoded: sda_oen remains released initially while scl_oen is released, then sda_oen drives low while SCL remains released, followed by the START sequence completion and return to idle. This is the supported-command side of the required decode behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare the observed sda_oen waveform and idle/start_sequence probes against the START reference sequence; verify no other command signature occurs.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START command, wait for idle=1, then with ena=1 and a released-high bus present cmd=STOP (0010) through a clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: The STOP command is decoded: sda_oen drives SDA low, then the sequence releases SCL and finally releases SDA while SCL is high before returning to idle. This is the supported-command side of the required decode behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare sda_oen and scl_oen sampled after each posedge with the STOP reference waveform, using stop_sequence and idle to delimit the sequence; verify the waveform is not a START, READ, or WRITE signature.

elements.stimulus: After reset and idle detection, keep ena=1, provide a released-high SCL bus with the external SDA value controlled for a valid read bit, present cmd=READ (1000) through a clk_en tick, and allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: The READ command is decoded: sda_oen is released for the read sequence, scl_oen is released during the read sampling window, and the controller returns to idle after the read bit cycle. This is the supported-command side of the required decode behavior.
elements.check_method: Use read_sequence and read_sample_window to delimit the operation and compare the registered sda_oen/scl_oen waveform against the READ reference model; verify SDA is not driven with the WRITE signature.

elements.stimulus: After reset and idle detection, set ena=1, set din=0, present cmd=WRITE (0100) through a clk_en tick, and provide normal released-high and low SCL phases until completion.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE command is decoded: sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0 during the write bit, releases SCL for the high phase, then completes and returns to idle without arbitration loss. This is the supported-command side of the required decode behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare sda_oen and scl_oen at every timing phase against a WRITE(din=0) reference model, using write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase; verify cmd_ack occurs only at completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset and idle detection, set ena=1, set din=1, present cmd=WRITE (0100) through a clk_en tick, and keep SDA externally high during the released write high phase.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE command is decoded: sda_oen releases SDA for din=1 during the write bit, performs the released-high write phase without arbitration loss, then completes and returns to idle. This is the supported-command side of the required decode behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare the sda_oen/scl_oen sequence with a WRITE(din=1) reference model and verify write_stable_high_phase and sda_chk occur; verify no START, STOP, or READ signature is produced.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the bus released high, wait until idle=1, present cmd=NOP (0000) for multiple clk_en ticks, then return cmd to NOP.
elements.expected_response: cmd=NOP is decoded as no operation: the FSM remains idle, sda_oen and scl_oen remain released, no command-specific SDA sequence starts, and no command-complete pulse is generated. This is the no-operation side of the required decode behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor idle, start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, write_sequence, sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack over all driven clk_en ticks; assert idle and released outputs continuously with no sequence probe activation.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the bus released high, wait until idle=1, present an unsupported cmd value such as 0011 through several clk_en ticks, and then replace it with NOP.
elements.expected_response: The unsupported command is treated as no operation: the FSM remains idle, sda_oen and scl_oen stay released, and no command-specific SDA sequence or cmd_ack is produced. This is the contrasting non-supported-command side of the required decode behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare the output and probe trace against the idle/no-op reference model across every clk_en tick; assert no start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, write_sequence, or cmd_ack activity.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=16'h0000, ensure the FSM is idle and both bus lines are released, then drive cmd=4'b0001 (START) through an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case is false: idle deasserts and start_sequence asserts, indicating that the recognized START command entered the corresponding command sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset and command acceptance, compare the idle and start_sequence probes against the reference FSM transition; require start_sequence=1 and idle=0 after the enabled tick.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=16'h0000, ensure the FSM is idle and the bus is in a valid STOP-command starting condition, then drive cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) through an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case is false: idle deasserts and stop_sequence asserts, indicating that the recognized STOP command entered the corresponding command sequence.
elements.check_method: Sample idle and stop_sequence after the command-acceptance posedge and compare with the reference FSM; require stop_sequence=1 and idle=0.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=16'h0000, ensure the FSM is idle with the bus released, then drive cmd=4'b1000 (READ) through an enabled clock tick while providing a released or externally driven SCL/SDA bus.
elements.expected_response: Holding case is false: idle deasserts and read_sequence asserts, indicating that the recognized READ command entered the corresponding command sequence.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed idle and read_sequence probes with the reference FSM immediately after command acceptance; require read_sequence=1 and idle=0.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=16'h0000, ensure the FSM is idle, set din to either 0 or 1, then drive cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) through an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding case is false: idle deasserts and write_sequence asserts, indicating that the recognized WRITE command entered the corresponding command sequence.
elements.check_method: After the enabled command-acceptance posedge, compare idle and write_sequence to the reference FSM; require write_sequence=1 and idle=0 for both din values.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=16'h0000, ensure the FSM is idle, then drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for multiple enabled clock ticks.
elements.expected_response: Holding case is true: idle remains asserted and start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence remain deasserted; no command sequence is entered.
elements.check_method: Monitor all five probes after every enabled posedge during the command hold and compare against the reference model; require idle=1 and all four sequence probes=0 throughout.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=16'h0000, ensure the FSM is idle, and successively present every unsupported 4-bit cmd value (0011 and 0101 through 1111), holding each value across multiple enabled clock ticks with the FSM returned to idle between values.
elements.expected_response: Holding case is true for every unsupported value: idle remains asserted and start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence remain deasserted; no unsupported command causes a sequence transition.
elements.check_method: For each unsupported encoding, sample all five probes after each enabled tick and compare with the reference FSM; require idle=1 and all command-sequence probes=0 for the entire interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1 and cmd=4'b0001 (START) for command acceptance, then keep the bus released and run clocks until cmd_ack is observed.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the START sequence, scl_oen remains high (SCL released); sda_oen is initially high (SDA released) and then changes low while scl_oen remains high, producing the SDA-low-while-SCL-high START phase.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, use a temporal assertion on scl_oen and sda_oen: observe an initial released phase, followed before cmd_ack by sda_oen=0 while scl_oen=1, and confirm the pattern occurs within the START command interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the bus high, set cmd=4'b0001 (START) while ena=0 and hold ena low for longer than the normal START sequence duration, then return cmd to NOP.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case: because the START command is not accepted while ena is low, sda_oen and scl_oen remain released high; the required release-then-drive-low START pattern does not occur.
elements.check_method: During the ena=0 interval, sample registered sda_oen and scl_oen after each posedge and assert that no cycle has sda_oen=0 while scl_oen=1 and that neither output enable shows a START-sequence transition.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high and rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and issue cmd=0001 (START) while the FSM is idle. Wait for the START sequence to generate SDA low while SCL is high, then observe the terminal completion phase and the following clock.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: after the generated START condition, scl_oen becomes low, the command FSM returns to idle, and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle and low on the next clock.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor the start_sequence and idle probes, compare scl_oen against the expected terminal phase, and assert that cmd_ack has one and only one consecutive high sample associated with the return to idle.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high and rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and issue cmd=0001 (START). After SDA has been pulled low for the START condition but before the normal terminal completion edge, assert nReset low asynchronously and hold it low through the next clock.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise side of the observed behavior: reset aborts the START sequence, so the normal terminal completion does not occur; scl_oen is released high, the FSM is idle, and cmd_ack does not pulse high.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen immediately after asynchronous reset and cmd_ack and idle after the next posedge; verify no cmd_ack high pulse occurs and no post-reset terminal START phase drives scl_oen low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, present a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, and issue cmd=0010 (STOP) on a rising edge. Continue clocking until the STOP command completes.
elements.expected_response: The STOP sequence first drives SDA low with sda_oen=0 while SCL remains driven low with scl_oen=0. It then releases SCL by changing scl_oen to 1 while sda_oen remains 0. After the bus SCL is high, it releases SDA by changing sda_oen to 1, generating the STOP transition, and subsequently produces one cmd_ack pulse. This is the required `shows` side of REQ-0133.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, record stop_sequence, scl_oen, sda_oen, the resolved SCL line, and cmd_ack. Assert the ordered temporal sequence sda_oen=0; then scl_oen=1 while sda_oen=0 and resolved SCL=1; then sda_oen=1 only after resolved SCL=1. Assert exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=0010 (STOP), and model the open-drain bus with sda_i=1 and scl_i held low externally after the controller releases scl_oen. Keep scl_i=0 for several enabled timing ticks, then release the external SCL hold by setting scl_i=1 and continue clocking through command completion.
elements.expected_response: During the externally held-low interval, scl_oen becomes 1 but sda_oen remains 0; SDA is not released while the resolved SCL line is low. Once filtered SCL becomes high, sda_oen changes to 1 and the STOP transition is generated, followed by one cmd_ack pulse. The contrasting `otherwise` side—SDA release before SCL is high—must not occur.
elements.check_method: Monitor every posedge during stop_sequence and compare sda_oen against the resolved, filtered SCL level. Assert that any transition of sda_oen from 0 to 1 occurs only after scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL is high; assert no premature SDA release while filtered SCL is low, then check the final cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=0010 (STOP) while the bus is released high. Allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, observe filtered SCL high, then release SDA; keep reset inactive and do not issue another command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the STOP terminal phase completes, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock, then returns low; scl_oen and sda_oen are both high after completion.
elements.check_method: Use a clocking-block monitor after each posedge to detect the STOP terminal phase and compare cmd_ack against a one-cycle pulse immediately following it; verify the idle probe is high after completion and remains high absent a new command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=0010 (STOP) with SDA initially released high, then externally hold SCL low after the controller releases SCL so the STOP sequence cannot reach the phase that releases SDA while SCL is high; keep the stretch active for multiple enabled timing ticks.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because the STOP command has not completed, the FSM does not return to idle and cmd_ack does not pulse high; the command remains active and waits for filtered SCL to become high.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered SCL level, stop_sequence/active_command probes, idle probe, and cmd_ack after each settled posedge. Assert that throughout the externally held-low interval there is no cmd_ack high pulse and no transition to idle.

elements.stimulus: From reset, keep ena high, hold the bus released and SCL high, drive cmd=1000 (READ), and wait for an enabled clk_en tick while the command FSM is idle. Continue providing normal filtered SCL timing and an external SDA data value through the READ data-bit phase, without asserting reset or causing arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: after READ acceptance and while read_sequence is active during the READ data-bit phase, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA for the external slave; cmd_ack remains 0 until the READ sequence completes.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, correlate read_sequence/read_sample_window with sda_oen and cmd_ack. Assert sda_oen==1 throughout the READ data-bit phase and assert cmd_ack==0 until the terminal READ phase, followed by exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena high, drive cmd=0010 (STOP) and wait for an enabled clk_en tick, with the bus initially released. Observe the STOP sequence through its SDA-low phase before SCL and then SDA are released.
elements.expected_response: Outside case of shows: while the controller is in the STOP command phase rather than the READ data-bit phase, sda_oen may reflect the other command's behavior and is expected to be 0 during the STOP SDA-low phase; REQ-0135 places no READ-release constraint on this phase.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use stop_sequence to identify the STOP SDA-low phase and compare sda_oen==0 there. Confirm the observation is outside read_sequence/read_sample_window, so this result is classified as the non-READ side of shows rather than as a violation of the READ requirement.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ (1000), and provide a released-high bus. Keep the external SCL and SDA lines high until the READ sequence reaches read_sample_window=1; then allow the filtered SCL rising edge to occur and continue clocks until the READ sampling window ends.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of observed_via.shows: while read_sample_window=1, scl_oen is 1, releasing SCL high; when the read window ends, scl_oen transitions to 0 and drives SCL low.
elements.check_method: Sample read_sequence/read_sample_window and scl_oen after each posedge clk. Assert that scl_oen remains 1 for the complete read_sample_window interval and that the first subsequent registered SCL output-enable value is 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ (1000), and provide a released-high bus. Wait until read_sample_window=1 and scl_oen=1, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the read window can complete; release nReset and do not issue another command.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case of observed_via.shows: asynchronous reset aborts the READ window, scl_oen is reset to 1, and no normal read-window completion transition to scl_oen=0 occurs after the abort.
elements.check_method: Monitor read_sample_window and scl_oen around the asynchronous reset. Confirm the window is aborted and, from reset assertion through recovery without a new READ command, scl_oen never exhibits the required completed-window sequence of remaining 1 through the window followed by a transition to 0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a READ command while the bus is released. During the READ sample window, keep scl_i high long enough for the synchronizer and three-sample filter to produce a filtered SCL rising edge, and keep sda_i stable high so filtered SDA is high at that edge. Use clk_cnt=0 to permit enabled progress on every clock, and wait for the filtered edge and registered dout update.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the clock processing the rising edge of filtered SCL, dout updates on the following registered observation to the filtered SDA value, 1. The update must correspond to the filtered SDA value at that filtered SCL rising edge, not merely to the raw sda_i value or an arbitrary READ phase.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for two-stage synchronization, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered-edge detection. At each modeled sscl rising edge, compare post-posedge dout with modeled ssda; specifically require dout=1 for this edge and verify the update occurs with the specified registered latency.

elements.stimulus: Initialize dout to 1, set ena=1, and issue a READ command. During the READ sample window, have an external participant hold scl_i low so that filtered SCL remains low and no filtered SCL rising edge occurs; keep sda_i low or toggle it without allowing a filtered SCL rising edge. Hold the condition for multiple enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no rising edge of filtered SCL occurs, dout retains its previous value of 1; it must not update to the filtered SDA value or to another value during the interval without the triggering edge.
elements.check_method: Monitor the modeled sscl transition stream and confirm it contains no rising edge while the stimulus is applied. Compare dout after every settled posedge against its value before the interval and require it remains 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ (1000), and issue the command on a posedge while the bus is released high. Keep SDA released during the READ sequence, allow filtered SCL to rise, drive the external SDA value to 1 before the filtered SCL rising edge, then allow the read bit cycle to proceed through its SCL-low terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: after the READ bit cycle completes, the command FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock; cmd_ack is low on the following clock.
elements.check_method: Use the idle probe and a cycle-accurate monitor of cmd_ack. Compare the observed terminal transition and one-clock pulse against a reference READ-sequence model using the enabled timing ticks, filtered SCL rising edge, and registered output latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ (1000), and let the READ sequence reach the read sampling phase with SCL released high. Before the read bit cycle reaches its terminal completion phase, assert nReset=0 asynchronously and hold it through the would-be command-completion clock, then release nReset without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of the observed behavior: because the READ bit cycle was aborted before completion, cmd_ack does not assert for that READ command; reset returns the FSM to idle and leaves cmd_ack low.
elements.check_method: Sample cmd_ack asynchronously during reset and after each subsequent posedge, and check the idle probe after reset release. Assert that no cmd_ack pulse is associated with the aborted READ, contrasting it with the one-clock completion pulse required when the READ bit cycle actually completes.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), din=0, and clk_cnt to a small nonzero value. Keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high, issue the WRITE command on a clock edge, and hold din=0 through the WRITE data-bit drive phase before the corresponding SCL high phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit drive phase, sda_oen is 0, so the active-low open-drain interface drives SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the required behavior; sda_oen must not be 1 and release SDA in this phase.
elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence and phase probes to identify the data-bit drive interval, then sample the registered sda_oen after each posedge in that interval and compare it with the reference mapping sda_oen = ~din. Confirm the observed bus SDA is low when externally released.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), din=1, and clk_cnt to a small nonzero value. Keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high, issue the WRITE command on a clock edge, and hold din=1 through the WRITE data-bit drive phase before the corresponding SCL high phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit drive phase, sda_oen is 1, so SDA is released high rather than driven low. This is the din=1 side of the required behavior; sda_oen must not be 0 and drive SDA low in this phase.
elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence and phase probes to identify the data-bit drive interval, then sample the registered sda_oen after each posedge in that interval and compare it with the reference mapping sda_oen = ~din. Confirm the observed bus SDA remains high when no external participant drives it low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, present cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=0, and continue driving din=0 until the WRITE command completes.
elements.expected_response: During the active WRITE data-bit phase after the WRITE sequence begins and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0, meaning the master drives SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the required sda_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence probe to identify the active data-bit phase, then sample registered sda_oen after each posedge until cmd_ack; compare against sda_oen==0 throughout that phase and require no mismatch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, present cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=1, and continue driving din=1 until the WRITE command completes.
elements.expected_response: During the active WRITE data-bit phase after the WRITE sequence begins and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, meaning the master releases SDA so the bus can be pulled high. This is the din=1 side of the required sda_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence probe to identify the active data-bit phase, then sample registered sda_oen after each posedge until cmd_ack; compare against sda_oen==1 throughout that phase and require no mismatch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1, configure clk_cnt=1, hold the external SCL and SDA lines high, set din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100 while idle. Keep the external SDA high through the WRITE stable-high phase so arbitration succeeds.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE sequence reaches the stable high phase with scl_oen=1, then pulls SCL low with scl_oen=0, returns the FSM to idle, and asserts cmd_ack=1 for exactly one clock before deasserting it.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked waveform assertion/reference model to verify the ordered scl_oen transition 1-to-0 after write_stable_high_phase becomes active, followed by idle and a single-cycle cmd_ack pulse with no al assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold ena=1, configure clk_cnt=1, set din=1, issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100 while idle, and externally hold SDA low when the controller reaches the released stable SCL-high phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting, non-holding side of REQ-0141: arbitration loss aborts the WRITE before the required completion sequence, so scl_oen does not show the required release-then-pull-low completion phase and cmd_ack does not pulse for the aborted command; both output enables are released after the abort.
elements.check_method: Use assertions correlated with write_stable_high_phase and sda_chk to check that al becomes asserted, no cmd_ack pulse occurs, and no post-phase scl_oen=0 completion transition is attributed to successful WRITE completion.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=START from idle and run until the START sequence reaches its phase that pulls SDA low while SCL remains released.
elements.expected_response: During the START SDA-drive phase, the expected side of shows is observed: sda_oen=0, scl_oen=1, scl_o=0, and sda_o=0. The output enables use active-low open-drain control and the drive outputs remain constant low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from command acceptance through the SDA-drive phase, compare scl_o and sda_o against 0 and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against the phase-level reference model; require the sampled phase to match sda_oen=0 and scl_oen=1.

elements.stimulus: Continue the accepted START command from TP-0000 until its phase that releases SDA and SCL, then wait for cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting release side of shows is observed: sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1, while scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 remain constant. Neither line is actively pulled low in this phase.
elements.check_method: Monitor every settled posedge through START completion; assert both constant-low drive outputs and compare both output enables with the reference phase model, specifically requiring 1 for each released line.

elements.stimulus: After completing START and establishing a busy bus, issue cmd=STOP with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0; run until the STOP sequence drives SDA low while SCL is released.
elements.expected_response: During the STOP drive phase, the expected active-drive side of shows is observed: sda_oen=0 and scl_oen=1. scl_o and sda_o remain 0 throughout.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate STOP phase reference model and assert the four output values after each posedge; require the SDA drive/SCL release combination before the STOP release phase and no nonzero drive-output value.

elements.stimulus: Continue the STOP command until SCL is high and the controller releases SDA, then wait for the one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting release side of shows is observed: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 while SCL is released high. scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 remain constant rather than sourcing a high level.
elements.check_method: Sample the registered outputs after each posedge through STOP completion and compare them with the STOP reference sequence; explicitly check the release phase has both enables equal to 1 and both drive outputs equal to 0.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0; hold the external bus high and run through the WRITE bit's SDA setup and released SCL-high phase, then through the SCL-low phase to cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: The expected open-drain drive/release behavior is observed: SDA is actively pulled low for din=0 with sda_oen=0, SCL is released during its high phase with scl_oen=1, and SCL is actively pulled low during its low phase with scl_oen=0. scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 in all phases.
elements.check_method: Compare each registered output-enable value at every WRITE phase boundary against a reference model parameterized by din=0; assert that the external resolved lines are consistent with open-drain ownership and that both drive outputs are always 0.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1; hold SDA high externally during the released write phase and run through the SCL-high arbitration phase and subsequent SCL-low phase to cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting SDA release side of shows is observed: sda_oen=1 while transmitting din=1, scl_oen=1 during the released SCL-high phase, and scl_oen=0 during the SCL-low phase. scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0; no arbitration loss occurs because the external SDA value is high.
elements.check_method: Use assertions tied to write_sequence and write_stable_high_phase to compare sda_oen and scl_oen against the write reference model; check both constant-low drive outputs on every settled posedge and require al=0 and eventual cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ, provide a stable external SDA value of 1, allow the read sample window with SCL released, then allow the controller to pull SCL low and complete the command.
elements.expected_response: During the READ sample window the expected release side of shows is observed: sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1. In the following low phase scl_oen=0 while SDA remains released with sda_oen=1. scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 throughout.
elements.check_method: Monitor read_sequence and read_sample_window, compare output enables to the READ reference phase sequence, and assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 on every sampled cycle through cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Start a WRITE with din=1 and ena=1, then externally force SDA low during the released SCL-high phase to cause arbitration loss; observe outputs through the abort.
elements.expected_response: The open-drain behavior remains valid on the abort path: before and at arbitration loss, scl_o and sda_o are constant 0 and output enables are only 0 for actively driven-low phases or 1 for released phases. After al asserts, both scl_oen and sda_oen become 1, no cmd_ack is generated, and both lines are released.
elements.check_method: Inject the filtered SDA-low condition only while write_stable_high_phase is active, then compare every output-enable transition and status output against the arbitration-loss reference model; assert constant-low drive outputs and absence of cmd_ack for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue a START command, and continue clocking until the START sequence completes. Observe the initial released phase, the phase where SDA is pulled low while SCL is released, and the phase where SCL is subsequently pulled low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during released phases, scl_oen=1 and/or sda_oen=1, selecting released operation for the corresponding line. Contrasting active case: when a line is required to be pulled low, its enable is 0 (sda_oen=0 during the START SDA-low phase and scl_oen=0 during the following SCL-low phase). At every clock-edge observation throughout the sequence, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0.
elements.check_method: Use clock-edge assertions over the complete START transaction: assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 unconditionally; compare each observed scl_oen and sda_oen value against the reference START phase, asserting 1 for released phases and 0 for active pull-low phases. Resolve each bus line as low when its enable is 0 and high otherwise, with no external pull-down present.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START command, then issue a STOP command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 while the external bus remains released high. During STOP, drive the sequence through SDA low, SCL released high, and finally SDA released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting active case: during the STOP low phase, sda_oen=0 selects active pull-low operation for SDA. Holding/released case: after the low phase, scl_oen=1 releases SCL and then sda_oen=1 releases SDA while SCL is high. At every clock-edge observation, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 regardless of either output-enable state.
elements.check_method: Assert the constant-drive outputs are zero on every sampled clock edge. Use a phase-aware scoreboard for STOP that requires sda_oen=0 during the driven-low phase, scl_oen=1 during the released-SCL phase, and sda_oen=1 during the final released-SDA phase; independently verify the resolved bus levels match the selected enable states.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a valid START command with ena high and clk_cnt set to a value that permits FSM progress. Observe the START phase in which SDA is pulled low while SCL remains released; sample after each posedge update.
elements.expected_response: While sda_oen is low, the resolved SDA line is driven low, corresponding to the low-enable side of REQ-0144. During the same phase scl_oen remains high and SCL is released rather than driven low. The registered sda_o and scl_o outputs remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: Use an open-drain bus model with a pull-up: compare the resolved SDA line against 0 whenever sda_oen=0, and verify the resolved SCL line can remain high when scl_oen=1. Also assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a valid START command with ena high and allow the command sequence to reach its subsequent low-SCL phase, sampling after each posedge update.
elements.expected_response: While scl_oen is low, the resolved SCL line is driven low, corresponding to the low-enable side of REQ-0144. The corresponding SDA output-enable follows the START sequence and is checked independently; the registered scl_o and sda_o outputs remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: Use an open-drain bus model with a pull-up and compare the resolved SCL line against 0 whenever scl_oen=0. Confirm the low line is caused by the low output enable, and assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it, and leave the controller idle with ena high and the external SCL and SDA pull-ups enabled. Observe the registered outputs after reset release and subsequent clock edges.
elements.expected_response: With scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, neither line is driven low: the resolved SCL and SDA lines remain high through the pull-ups. This is the contrasting high-enable side of REQ-0144. scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 despite the lines being released.
elements.check_method: Check the resolved open-drain bus lines are high when both output enables are high, verify scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1, and assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. Ensure this differs from the low-enable cases rather than treating the constant drive outputs alone as evidence.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold external SCL and SDA drivers released, then issue cmd=START while idle. Wait through the START sequence until the phase in which both SCL and SDA are released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1; the open-drain bus model observes SCL=1 and SDA=1 because the external pull-ups drive both released lines high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare scl_oen and sda_oen with the START-sequence reference model and calculate each bus line as high when the corresponding enable is 1 and no external device drives it low.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=START while idle and keep the external bus otherwise released. Continue clocking through the START sequence, observing first the phase that pulls SDA low while SCL remains released and then the phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: when sda_oen=0, SDA is driven low rather than released high; when scl_oen=0, SCL is driven low rather than released high. The corresponding released line remains high only while its output enable is 1.
elements.check_method: Use the START-sequence reference model to identify each output-enable phase, then compare the observed enables and open-drain bus levels: enable 0 must produce a low line and enable 1 must produce a pull-up-high line in the absence of an external low drive.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Present START while idle and hold the command inputs stable until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: The START command sequence executes to its terminal phase, then cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle. cmd_ack is low before the terminal completion cycle and low again on the immediately following clock.
elements.check_method: Use a clock-aligned scoreboard keyed to the observed START sequence and its terminal phase; compare cmd_ack on every posedge from command acceptance through one cycle after completion and assert a one-cycle pulse with no early or repeated assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish a completed or busy bus context as needed, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, present cmd=STOP while idle, and keep the command inputs stable until the STOP sequence completes.

That sentence is the target. Stage what the CHECK says it did not see, which is not always what the activation above describes.

What must then be true: the corresponding released SCL or SDA line is driven high by the external pull-up resistor
